papers.title: HMGB1 signalling in Alzheimer's disease: pathogenic roles and therapeutic prospects.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative condition marked by the gradual loss of neurons, especially in the hippocampus and cerebral cortex. This neuronal loss results in cognitive decline, memory problems, and changes in behaviour. It accounts for roughly 90% of all cases, making it the most common reason for dementia worldwide, with a marked rise in its occurrence as one ages. AD is pathologically marked by the presence of intracellular neurofibrillary tangles composed of hyperphosphorylated tau protein and the formation of extracellular amyloid-β plaques. Along with these defining characteristics, oxidative stress and chronic neuroinflammation, which are triggered by prolonged astrocyte and microglia activation and excessive reactive oxygen species production, play crucial roles in the development of the illness. The majority of cases of AD are sporadic late-onset illness, but the less common familial variant is linked to mutations in the APP, PSEN1, and PSEN2 genes that cause aberrant amyloid-β formation. High mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) is a crucial modulator of neuroinflammation in AD, according to new research. By activating the receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE) and Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), HMGB1, especially in its pro-inflammatory disulfide state, hinders memory and learning. RAGE/CaMKKβ-AMPK, ERK1/2, GSK-3β, NF-κB, MAPKs, and NLRP3 inflammasome cascades are among the overlapping downstream signalling pathways that these receptors initiate. Together, these pathways induce tau hyperphosphorylation, amyloid-β buildup, and persistent inflammatory responses. Therefore, a viable treatment approach for reducing neuroinflammation and associated pathologies with AD. is to target HMGB1-mediated signalling networks.

papers.title: Vorinostat ameliorates cognitive impairment and Tau pathology in an AAV-P301L-Tau-induced tauopathy mouse model: insights into neuroinflammation and PI3K/AKT/GSK3β signaling.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder with significant sex-related differences, exhibiting a higher incidence rate in elderly women. Tau pathology has been implicated in sex-associated differences in AD susceptibility and disease progression, contributing to differential pathological burden between males and females. Vorinostat (SAHA), a histone deacetylase inhibitor (HDACi) used in cancer treatment, has shown potential therapeutic effects in various neurological and psychiatric disorders; however, the mechanisms underlying its regulation of tau-associated pathology remain poorly understood, with limited evidence regarding its effects in tau-related neurodegenerative conditions. In this study, we investigated the effects of SAHA treatment on an AAV-P301L-Tau-induced tauopathy model. In vivo, we observed that SAHA administration significantly improved p-Tau levels in the hippocampus and cortex of mice, reduced microglial activation and neuronal damage, and alleviated tauopathy-associated cognitive impairments. Our findings revealed sex-associated differences in Tau-related pathological alterations, with female mice exhibiting greater pathological changes and differential responses to SAHA treatment in several molecular and histological indicators. Further combined in vivo and in vitro experiments revealed that SAHA was associated with modulation of the PI3K/AKT/GSK3β signaling pathway, suppression of NF-κB activation, and attenuation of neuroinflammatory responses, including reductions in experimentally measured inflammatory markers such as interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumour necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α). These molecular alterations may represent important regulatory components contributing to the neuroprotective effects of SAHA, rather than acting as the sole determinants of its therapeutic efficacy. In summary, these results indicate that SAHA can improve Tau-associated pathological alterations in an AAV-P301L-Tau-induced tauopathy model. The potential mechanisms may involve coordinated regulation of multiple pathological processes, including modulation of Tau phosphorylation, neuroinflammatory responses, and aging-associated signaling pathways. The observed sex-dependent responses to SAHA provide additional insights into the potential influence of biological sex on HDACi-based therapeutic strategies, although the molecular mechanisms underlying these differences require further investigation.

papers.title: Are mouse models of Alzheimer's disease truly flawed, or are we misusing them?
papers.abstract: The first transgenic mouse models of Alzheimer's disease (AD) developed in the 1990 s were hailed as a major breakthrough. As newer generations of models have emerged over the decades after, they still face growing criticism for translating poorly into clinical outcomes, even if the effects of newer therapeutic compounds, including monoclonal antibodies, align well with those seen in mice. Like any disease model, AD mice have substantial limitations. The real issue is that they are often treated as miniature humans with AD, which they are not. Overreliance on specific pathogen-free (SPF) housing may also blunt immune-related endpoints and compromise translational relevance. The impact of biological sex and ambient temperature may also differ between animal models and humans. In this review, we argue that despite these limitations, they remain highly useful for specific scientific questions and preclinical development. They are far better suited for pharmacokinetic and biodistribution studies, and for testing target engagement in vivo on well-defined neuropathological processes. Thus, while criticisms of these models are justified, researchers have often used them with misaligned objectives. As discussed herein, these models should not be discarded, but used more thoughtfully, in ways that align with their true strengths.

papers.title: Depression and amyloid-β across CSF, PET, and plasma biomarkers: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease is increasingly defined by biomarker evidence of amyloid-β and tau pathology, sharpening questions about whether late-life depression contributes to, or instead reflects, this pathology. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published between 2000 and 2025 that compared amyloid-β biomarkers in adults with and without depression, with depression defined by validated clinical diagnoses or symptom rating scales. Twenty-four studies were included, spanning three biomarker sources: cerebrospinal fluid, positron emission tomography imaging, and plasma. Across all sources, the pooled difference in amyloid-β burden between depressed and non-depressed individuals was small and clustered near zero, indicating only a weak, statistically non-significant tendency toward higher amyloid in depression. When the three sources were examined separately, each yielded a similar near-null result, although between-study heterogeneity was considerable for cerebrospinal fluid and plasma and moderate for imaging. Importantly, a prespecified subgroup analysis showed that imaging results diverged by quantification method: studies using the simpler standardized uptake value ratio clustered around zero, whereas the smaller group of studies using kinetic distribution volume ratio modelling showed a significant positive association, suggesting that methodological choices critically influence the observed relationship. Taken together, these findings indicate that depression is not consistently accompanied by greater amyloid-β burden across widely used biomarker platforms. The distribution volume ratio signal nonetheless raises the possibility of subtle associations that cruder methods may obscure, and suggests that depression may shape Alzheimer's disease trajectories more by modifying the clinical impact of amyloid than by altering its amount.

papers.title: The International Alliance on Brain Health (IABH): Bridging global efforts toward integrated brain and mental health plans and the promotion of local implementations.
papers.abstract: The convergence of neurological, psychiatric, neurodevelopmental, and public health approaches to brain health is reshaping global strategies for prevention, care, and policy. However, major gaps remain in the integration and implementation of brain and mental health frameworks across healthcare systems and regions. This paper describes the foundation and early development of the International Alliance on Brain Health (IABH), established in Switzerland in 2025 to promote interdisciplinary collaboration, reciprocal innovation, and implementation-oriented exchange between the global North and global South. Drawing on the Alliances founding meeting in Bern, its contribution as a partner to the World Brain Health Forum organized by the Paris Brain Institute, and its subsequent meeting in Buenos Aires, the paper outlines the Alliance's global positioning and priorities for translating brain health frameworks into practice. Key themes included integrated neurological and mental health approaches, prevention across the life course, digital innovation, brain capital, workforce development, and stronger inclusion of global South perspectives in international policy dialogue. The Alliance also emphasized bidirectional learning and locally adaptable implementation strategies aligned with WHO brain health frameworks. Under the joint patronage of the World Federation of Neurology and the World Psychiatric Association, the IABH represents an emerging platform for cross-continental collaboration in brain health.

papers.title: A promising therapeutic strategy reduces abnormal Aβ deposition and inhibits neuronal apoptosis via FGF17 ameliorating AD-like neurodegeneration.
papers.abstract:
AIMS: We explore a possible association between dysregulated FGF17 expression and the pathogenesis underlying AD, and discovery efficacious therapeutic strategies.
METHODS: We measured FGF17 levels in serum from AD patients, and selected APP/PS1 mice as well as SH-SY5Y cells stimulated with Aβ1-42 for 24 h as the AD model. Through AAV9-mediated gene delivery (stereotactic injection) or exogenous human recombinant protein administering, we investigated the effects of FGF17 on cell apoptosis phenotype, synaptic defects, and behavioral manifestations.
RESULTS: Our investigation demonstrated diminished FGF17 concentrations in the serum of individuals with AD. Comparable reductions in FGF17 levels appeared in SH-SY5Y cells treated with Aβ1-42 over a 24-hour period, as well as in APP/PS1 mouse brains. Subsequent experiments demonstrated that AAV9-mediated FGF17 gene delivery could alleviate the cognitive impairment of APP/PS1 mice. Moreover, abnormal Aβ deposition and neuronal apoptosis were reduced through FGF17 treatment; the strategy inhibited neuronal damage and synaptic defects. Concurrently, we confirmed that in the aforementioned biological process, the FGFR3/PI3K/AKT signaling pathway was activated. Inhibiting FGFR3 reduced the protective effect of FGF17.
CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the promising disease-modifying therapies for FGF17 in managing AD. Our research indicates that the approach plays a positive role in both cognitive function and histopathology.

papers.title: Chronic lead exposure disrupts copper redox homeostasis and aggravates neurodegeneration.
papers.abstract: Lead (Pb) represents a critical environmental health concern due to its profound impact on neurodegenerative processes. However, its specific influence on copper (Cu) redox states and the associated neurotoxic mechanisms remain inadequately understood. In this study, male wild-type C57BL/6 and 5xFAD Alzheimer's disease (AD) model mice were used to investigate how chronic low-dose Pb exposure (200 μg/L via drinking water) exacerbated AD-related pathology through perturbation of Cu homeostasis. Elemental analysis revealed that Pb exposure depleted essential cerebral metals, including Ca, Mg, Fe, and Zn. In contrast to these metals, Cu showed concurrent accumulation in both the brain and bloodstream, particularly in the ADPb group, consistent with disturbed Cu homeostasis in the AD background. In situ fluorescent imaging demonstrated that Pb exposure significantly disrupted the Cu(I)/Cu(II) valence balance within the hippocampus. While the unexposed AD brain showed relatively higher Cu(I) signals, Pb exposure shifted the fluorescence pattern toward Cu(II). Behavioral assessments further indicated that Pb exposure was associated with reduced locomotor activity, anxiety-like responses, and accelerated spatial memory decay in AD mice. Histopathological and immunofluorescence evaluations structurally confirmed these functional deficits, revealing disorganized hippocampal cytoarchitecture, myelin loss, and accelerated Aβ plaque deposition in the ADPb group. Ultimately, these findings demonstrated that environmental Pb exacerbated AD progression not solely through direct physical toxicity, but fundamentally by disrupting the in situ Cu(II)/Cu(I) redox equilibrium. This study highlights Cu redox imbalance as a potential mediator linking Pb exposure with AD progression and warrants further biochemical validation.

papers.title: STAT3 mediated the isoleucine-induced Alzheimer's disease progression.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder that significantly impacts millions globally, with rising prevalence among the aging population, emphasizing the need for effective interventions. Isoleucine, a branched-chain amino acid, crosses the blood-brain barrier and plays a role in various neurological disorders. In this study, we investigated the association of isoleucine with AD traits using the BXD mouse reference population, revealing significant correlations with Y-maze performance, anxiety assays, contextual fear conditioning, and the age of onset for working memory deficits. In vitro, exogenous isoleucine supplementation in HT22 and PC12 cells increased amyloid precursor protein (APP) and phosphorylated tau (p-tau) levels. Subsequent analysis identified 2,000 probes correlated with isoleucine and revealed STAT3 as a candidate downstream regulator. Overexpression of STAT3 increased APP and p-tau levels, and STAT3 inhibition abolished this effect, suggesting that isoleucine modulates AD progression via STAT3 activation. Mendelian randomization analysis further supported a causal relationship between elevated isoleucine levels and AD risk. This work provides insights into isoleucine as a potential risk factor for AD and identifies STAT3 as a mediator of isoleucine-related AD susceptibility.

papers.title: Association of hypoxic burden with brain atrophy in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a common comorbidity in Alzheimer's Disease (AD) and may exacerbate neurodegeneration. This study investigates the association between a novel metric of OSA severity-hypoxic burden (HB)-and measures of AD-related neurodegeneration.
METHODS: In this retrospective exploratory study, patients with AD at stage 3 and stage 4 (NIA-AA 2018 criteria), enrolled at a Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases, underwent a complete sleep assessment including polysomnography and 3 T brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging. Correlation analyses were conducted between HB and brain volumes.
RESULTS: Twenty-two patients (36.4% males, mean age 69.8 ± 7.5) were enrolled. OSA was diagnosed in 40.9% of patients. HB inversely correlated with left hippocampus (ρ = -0.553, p = 0.02) and left amygdala (ρ = -0.496, p = 0.04) volumes. AD patients with OSA showed significantly reduced left hippocampal volume than those without OSA (p = 0.038).
CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights that greater OSA severity, measured by HB, correlates with left hippocampus and amygdala atrophy, suggesting a possible association between chronic hypoxia and neurodegeneration in AD.

papers.title: Cell-specific expression of APP and GABABR1 isoforms in wild-type and the APP NL-G-F mouse model of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Amyloid precursor protein (APP) is a type I transmembrane protein that undergoes proteolytic processing to generate amyloid-β, the main component of amyloid plaques found in brains with Alzheimer's disease (AD). APP proteolytic processing also generates soluble APP alpha (sAPPα) which modulates synaptic transmission and neurite outgrowth through the γ-aminobutyric acid type B receptor (GABABR). sAPPα specifically binds the 1a isoform of GABABR subunit 1 (R1a) which contains two sushi domains absent in R1b. Here, we define the cell type-specific expression patterns of APP and GABABR1a in the brain and assess their alterations in the APP NL-G-F model of AD. We determined relative RNA levels of R1a and R1b isoforms in oligodendrocytes, microglia, endothelial cells, astrocytes, and neurons in adult mice using two approaches. We developed an isoform-specific RNAseq analysis workflow to probe publicly available datasets. We also isolated these cell types from a single mouse brain and performed RT-qPCR with isoform-specific primers. APP and GABABR1 isoforms were differentially expressed among cell types. APP and GABABR1a expression were highest in oligodendrocytes. In contrast, GABABR1b expression was highest in astrocytes. While microglia expressed relatively low levels of GABABR, they showed the greatest change in GABABR expression in the APP NL-G-F mouse model, with alterations that were both sex- and age-specific. Together, our findings identify candidate cell types in which future studies may investigate the potential role of APP-GABABR signaling in health and AD.

papers.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Signaling in Learning and Memory: Evidence, Mechanisms, and Therapeutic Implications.
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is primarily known for its role in glucose homeostasis and food intake control, and GLP-1 analogs (either as monotherapy or dual agonists) are commonly used for type 2 diabetes and obesity treatment in humans. Beyond these functions, the GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) is widely expressed throughout the brain, including in the hippocampus (HPC) and interconnected regions that contribute to learning and memory processes. Here we review emerging evidence supporting a role for GLP-1 signaling in promoting learning and memory function, particularly in dementia and other conditions that manifest with HPC dysfunction. Evidence is synthesized from preclinical rodent models revealing that GLP-1 analog treatment improves deficits in memory function and HPC neuronal signaling processes in various models of dementia, aging, and metabolic disruption. While findings from human clinical trials and meta-analyses also show promise for GLP-1 analog-based treatment for memory disorders, results thus far are mixed, with many studies underpowered and/or lacking comprehensive memory evaluation. We describe several distinct yet non-mutually exclusive neurobiological mechanisms by which GLP-1R signaling can enhance memory, including blood-brain barrier penetration and direct action on HPC GLP-1Rs, improved peripheral and central insulin sensitivity, vagus nerve GLP-1R activation, and peripheral metabolic and inflammatory improvements. We conclude by emphasizing important considerations for future clinical trials for GLP-1 analogs in the treatment of Alzheimer's disease and other memory disorders, including focusing on metabolically vulnerable individuals, stratifying results by cardiovascular and metabolic status, and leveraging existing GLP-1 analogs and drug delivery approaches toward maximizing bioavailability and brain penetrance.

papers.title: Single molecule, dual actions: GSK-3β/AChE dual inhibition for Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: The pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) is closely related with glycogen synthase kinase 3β (GSK-3β) and acetylcholinesterase (AChE). Our previous work verified that GL10a displayed superior GSK-3β inhibitory and neuroprotective activities relative to Tideglusib. Accordingly, a molecular hybridization strategy was applied to design and synthesize a series of dual target inhibitors against GSK-3β and AChE by conjugating GL10a and carbamate fragment of Rivastigmine's pharmacophore. After in vitro evaluations, the compound AJ-4 was screened as the most remarkable compound with potent inhibitory activities against GSK-3β (IC50: 4.7 nM) and AChE (IC50: 2.97 μM). Meanwhile, in vitro and in vivo data revealed that the optimal compound AJ-4 with excellent enzyme selectivity could decrease amyloid precursor protein (APP) and phosphorylated Tau expressions and increase phosphorylated GSK-3β levels. With favorable pharmacokinetic characteristics and tissue distribution, AJ-4 obviously ameliorated scopolamine-induced learning and memory impairments and alleviated hippocampal neuronal injury in AD mice. In conclusion, GSK-3β/AChE dual inhibitors represent a promising strategy for developing multi-target anti-AD drugs.

papers.title: From prediction to mechanism: Explainable AI uncovers plasma and CSF proteomic signatures of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) plasma and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteomics can distinguish AD from cognitively normal controls, but the generalizability of machine learning performance and the recurrence of biological signals across datasets require cautious interpretation. We developed an explainable artificial intelligence framework spanning two fluids and four ADNI proteomic datasets, covering 2082 modality specific samples, all analysed internally within ADNI. Phase 1 analysed plasma using a 119 analyte NULISA and targeted UPENN panel (n = 727; 216 CE, 511 controls). Phase 2 extended the analysis to CSF using SOMAscan7k, TMT-MS and targeted SET2, with Elecsys Aβ42, Aβ40, total tau and p-tau181 as anchor biomarkers. Only SOMAscan was subject-independent relative to Phase 1 plasma; TMT-MS and SET2 overlapped with Phase 1 for 96.0% and 97.7% of subjects and therefore are not independent replication cohorts. Under subject-level splits with fold internal preprocessing, we compared Elastic Net, Explainable Boosting Machines and gradient boosted trees with SHAP-based explanations. Among the candidate pipelines, we selected the pipeline with the highest held-out test ROC AUC for each platform; the selected values were 0.927 in plasma and 0.954-0.973 across the three CSF datasets. Because the same held out test performance was used for pipeline selection and headline reporting, these are optimistically selected single-holdout estimates, not unbiased estimates of generalizable or clinical performance. Explanations identified five recurring biological axes within ADNI: cholinergic (ACHE), tau/14-3-3 (YWHAG, YWHAZ, YWHAB, YWHAE), neuro-axonal (NEFL, NEFH), microglial/complement (CHIT1, SMOC1, CHI3L1, C7, CFH) and synaptic (NPTXR, NPTX2, DLG4, SYT5, VSNL1, ELAVL2). CSF analyses showed synaptic vesicle-cycle enrichment (q = 2 × 10-6), and CSF YWHAG correlated strongly with total tau (ρ = 0.87). Cross-fluid directional concordance was modest overall (54-57%) but increased to 73-80% among mapped analyte/protein rows reaching q < 0.05 in CSF. These findings provide hypothesis-generating, internally supported evidence within ADNI. Independent external cohorts with locked pipelines are required to evaluate generalizable performance and biological reproducibility; the overlapping TMT-MS and SET2 analyses should not be interpreted as independent replication.

papers.title: Cu2+-selective porphyrin probes with multifunctional anti-AD activities and the structural-activity insights from X-ray single crystal analysis.
papers.abstract: Metal ions play an important role in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). The aggregation of β-amyloid and oxidative stress caused by metal dyshomeostasis are important reasons for the progression of AD. Therefore, metal therapeutics have received increasing attention. In this work, two multifunctional near-infrared porphyrin probes (1 and 2) were designed and synthesized, and the single crystals of their Cu2+ complexes (1-Cu and 2-Cu) were obtained. Comprehensive biological activity evaluations demonstrated that 1, 2 possessed strong multifunctional anti-AD activities, including metal chelating, self-/Cu2+- induced Aβ1-42 aggregation inhibition, and in vitro/in vivo reactive oxygen species (ROS) elimination. Especially after coordination with copper, the cholinesterase inhibition and ROS elimination abilities were significantly increased. Notably, X-ray single crystal diffraction of 1, 1-Cu and 2-Cu provided crucial molecular-level structural information. Combined with molecular docking, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and molecular dynamics simulations, these crystallographic data fully elucidated the precise structure-activity relationships, revealing that the larger conjugated plane structure, differences in intermolecular forces and the picket-fence architecture significantly influenced the activities. Meanwhile, both probes exhibited highly selective fluorescence quenching responses to Cu2+ with very low cytotoxicity, indicating their promising potential as both therapeutic and diagnostic agents for AD.

papers.title: Screening molecular recognition element-based SWCNT optical sensors for the inflammatory cytokine TNF-α.
papers.abstract: TNF-α (Tumor Necrosis Factor) is a proinflammatory cytokine that amplifies inflammatory response and promotes leukocyte recruitment. TNF-α is primarily produced by activated macrophages, among others, in response to infection, inflammation, or tissue damage. Given its central role in normal and abnormal immune responses, it is the target of several therapeutics, such as adalimumab and etanercept. TNF-α is also a prognostic and diagnostic biomarker associated with rheumatoid arthritis, Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, several kidney diseases, cancers, type 2 diabetes, sepsis, and others. Because TNF-α levels change dynamically during inflammatory responses, tools capable of sensitive and spatially resolved detection could enable improved monitoring of immune activity and disease progression. Single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNT) are cylindrical carbon lattices that emit distinct near-infrared bandgap photoluminescence. In this work, we evaluated three aptamer-based sensor constructs, plus an additional two iterations of one aptamer sequence, and two antibody-based sensor constructs for TNF-α that use SWCNT near-infrared photoluminescence signal transduction. Several, but not all, of these aptamer and antibody-based sensors sensitively and selectively detected TNF-α in human and bovine serum in a physiologically relevant range, and we found that their sensing was impacted by both passivation and incorporating an exogenous quencher onto the aptamer sequence. This study highlights the importance and challenges of translating previously-validated molecular recognition elements to new detection conditions, in this case on the surface of SWCNT and in challenging serum conditions. It also validated a lead sensor, the VR11-SWCNT aptamer construct with or without quencher chemistry and with surface passivation, that builds upon constructs that failed in serum. These results demonstrate a strategy toward synthesis of nanoscale optical sensors capable of detecting TNF-α. We anticipate that the sensors evaluated here will have utility in both the diagnosis and study of inflammation-driven chronic disease, while the sensor assessment framework will help drive the broader field of molecularly specific diagnostics.

papers.title: AI-assisted integrative framework combining microarray data analysis and cerebrospinal fluid pharmacology for revealing molecular mechanism in Alzheimer's disease: A case study of Psoraleae Fructus.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by a gradual decline in cognitive function, with a complex pathogenesis involving multiple targets and signaling pathways, and current therapeutic strategies remain insufficient to achieve satisfactory outcomes. Psoraleae Fructus (PF) has been reported to exhibit potential therapeutic effects against AD. However, its multi-target mechanisms of action have not yet been systematically elucidated. In this study, an AI-assisted integrative computational and experimental framework was established to comprehensively investigate the molecular basis of PF intervention in AD. Targeted constituents of PF were first identified using UPLC-Q Exactive Orbitrap high-resolution mass spectrometry, followed by the integration of Artificial intelligence modeling, microarray data, and network pharmacology to screen hub targets. Cerebrospinal fluid-based pharmacological assays, together with molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, microarray validation, and western blot, were subsequently employed to validate. The results demonstrated that PF markedly modulated the expression of GSK3β and PPARγ, thereby regulating core AD-related pathological markers, including p-tau, Aβ42, β-secretase, and inflammatory mediators. Collectively, this study delineated a multi-target regulatory network underlying the anti-AD effects of PF and provided a robust theoretical foundation for its further translational investigation.

papers.title: A validated ligand binding assay for the determination of etalanetug, a novel anti-tau therapeutic antibody, in rats and monkeys for nonclinical pharmacokinetic studies.
papers.abstract: Etalanetug (E2814) is a novel human monoclonal antibody targeting tau that is currently being developed as a biotherapeutic for Alzheimer's disease. To inform pharmacological and toxicological evaluations in nonclinical settings and to guide dose selection for the first-in-human study, it is critical to characterize the pharmacokinetics (PK) of etalanetug. We have developed and validated a ligand-binding assay (LBA) for quantifying etalanetug in rat and monkey serum for use in nonclinical PK studies. Tau protein and anti-human immunoglobulin G antibody served as the capture and detection reagents, respectively. Using 10 µL of serum at a minimum dilution of 2000, etalanetug was quantifiable from 0.1 µg/mL in monkeys and 0.3 µg/mL in rats. Assay accuracy and precision, together with multiple serum stability assessments, demonstrated the robustness and reliability of the method. The assay was applied to PK studies in rats and monkeys. Following an intravenous dose of 30 mg/kg, etalanetug exhibited a biphasic decline in serum concentration with half-lives of 150-193 h in rats and monkeys. Incurred sample reanalysis further confirmed assay reproducibility. These results support the suitability of the developed LBA for nonclinical PK studies of etalanetug in both rats and monkeys.

papers.title: Early-onset axonal pathology and β-amyloidosis in human brains with hematological malignances and cardiovascular diseases.
papers.abstract: β-Amyloid (Aβ) and tau pathologies are hallmark lesions of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and they develop in human brain following differential spatiotemporal trajectories. Accordingly, young/adult-onset tau-independent β-amyloidosis is rare. We encountered four such cases among 397 banked brains, with the donors died of hematological malignances (blood cancers) or cardiovascular diseases. To explore the pathological implication, we examined 17 brains (10-87 year-old, y) from blood cancer patients and three (52-82 y) with cardiovascular diseases, focusing on vascular injury, axonal pathology and Aβ formation. Aβ plaques occurred in two adult brains (31 y, 63 y) with blood cancers and two (52 y, 65 y) with cardiovascular diseases in the absence of tau pathology. In the blood cancer brains, 17/17 had vascular injuries seen in hematoxylin-eosin stained sections, 13/17 had iron leakage, and 13/17 had axonal pathology. Malignant cell infiltration was found in 5/14 brains with myeloid, lymphocytic and lymphoma malignances, with light chain infiltration in 3/3 brains with multiple myeloma. In the cardiovascular disease brains, Aβ deposition primarily as diffuse plaques occurred in the cerebral cortex, with vascular and axonal pathologies in the white matter, striatum and internal capsule. Using a multi-labeling approach, the injury/stress induced axonal pathology was associated with β-amyloid processor protein and β-secretase 1 upregulation, but not with intra-axonal amyloid tracer staining. The current findings suggest that hematological malignances and cardiovascular diseases are risk conditions for early-onset cerebral axonal pathology and β-amyloidosis, potentially attributable to vascular injury.

papers.title: Brain weight across the adult lifespan in great apes.
papers.abstract: Reduction in brain weight is a hallmark feature of human aging, which is exacerbated in pathologies, such as Alzheimer's disease and other dementias. However, it remains unclear whether a decrease in brain weight with age reflects a vulnerability unique to the human lineage or represents a consequence of an extension of aging processes shared with other primates. To address this question, we examined age-related changes in brain weight across our closest living relatives, the great apes (chimpanzees, bonobos, gorillas, and orangutans). The sample spanned the full adult age range in each species and included individuals reaching ages comparable to those at which age-related brain changes become apparent in humans. Across species, brain weight did not show significant change throughout adulthood and into advanced age. The observed pattern held even when body weight was included in the analysis in a subsample of chimpanzees. Overall, these results indicate that marked brain weight loss is not a general feature of great ape aging and instead appears largely specific to humans, with implications for understanding susceptibility to late-life brain pathology.

papers.title: EOAD-Signature Atrophy Predicts Dementia in Early-Onset MCI due to Alzheimer Disease: An MRI-Based Prognostic Biomarker.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Early-onset Alzheimer disease (EOAD) is associated with substantial variability in clinical progression, and reliable biomarkers to predict the transition from mild cognitive impairment (MCI) to dementia remain limited. Structural MRI measures have demonstrated prognostic value in late-onset Alzheimer disease, but their utility for predicting progression in EOAD is less well understood. The goal was to examine whether baseline cortical atrophy predicts progression to dementia in patients with MCI because of EOAD.
METHODS: This study included a well-characterized cohort of patients with EOAD enrolled in the large multisite natural history Longitudinal Early-Onset Alzheimer's Disease Study. Participants underwent standardized clinical assessments and structural MRI at baseline. Participants were aged between 40 and 64 years with biomarker-supported sporadic EOAD at the MCI stage. Cortical atrophy was measured within the EOAD-signature, a set of predominantly parieto-temporal regions showing greater atrophy in EOAD than in controls. Clinical severity was measured with the global Clinical Dementia Rating. Cox proportional hazards models estimated the association between baseline EOAD-signature atrophy burden and the hazard of progression to dementia over time. We evaluated whether EOAD-signature atrophy improved prognostic performance beyond baseline clinical severity using likelihood ratio tests, Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), and Harrell concordance index.
RESULTS: A total of 130 patients with MCI due to EOAD (mean age 59.6 ± 4.1 years; 49% female) and 97 cognitively normal controls (mean age 56.9 ± 6.0 years; 64% female) were included. Greater baseline atrophy within the EOAD-signature predicted faster progression to dementia (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.24 per 1-SD increase in atrophy; 95% CI 1.13-1.37; p < 0.002). Adding EOAD-signature atrophy burden to a model including baseline clinical severity significantly improved model fit (ΔAIC = -4.5; likelihood ratio test p = 0.011).
DISCUSSION: Baseline cortical atrophy within the EOAD-signature predicts progression from MCI to dementia in EOAD and provides prognostic information beyond baseline clinical severity. These findings support the potential value of EOAD-signature atrophy as an MRI-based biomarker for individualized prognostication and clinical trial stratification.

papers.title: Uniform Dataset 3 Neuropsychological Battery: Czech Normative Study of a Battery assessing cognitive functioning in older adults.
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Uniform Data Set Neuropsychological Battery, version 3 (UDSNB 3), is a comprehensive, non-proprietary tool designed to assess cognitive domains relevant to neurodegenerative disorders, particularly Alzheimer's disease. This study aimed to establish Czech norms for the UDSNB 3, including the Lewy body disease module, using continuous norming methods.
METHODS: A normative sample of 171 cognitively healthy adults aged 50 - 95 years was recruited. Participants completed the Czech adaptation of the UDSNB 3. Continuous norming was performed using a semi-parametric approach. Education and age effects were examined, and selected scores were compared with previous Czech normative studies.
RESULTS: Cognitive performance generally declined with age across measures. Compared to previous Czech normative studies, differences were small and inconsistent across tests.
DISCUSSION: The present study provides the first Czech normative data for UDSNB 3 using continuous norming approach, supporting its clinical applicability. Continuous norming appears to be a viable approach for developing norms in contexts of countries with limited resources or smaller populations, where collecting large stratified samples of older adults can be difficult.

papers.title: Symptom-Guided Blood Biomarker Testing for Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: Introduction Blood-based biomarkers can accurately detect Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology, but symptom-guided testing approaches are understudied. This study evaluated the utility of early symptom and biomarker changes in predicting cognitive decline due to AD. Methods We analyzed data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative-2 (development, n=603) and -3 (validation, n=378). The primary outcome was 4-year progression to mild cognitive impairment or dementia associated with amyloid-beta neuropathology. Machine learning estimated baseline symptom burden from subjective ratings. Logistic regression calculated area under the curve (AUC), relative risk, and time-to-event. Results Symptom burden predicted clinical progression (AUC=0.79), which further improved with blood biomarkers (AUC=0.90). Participants with elevated symptoms and biomarkers had a progression incidence of 72.1% and a 19-fold higher progression risk. Findings replicated in validation. Conclusion Findings underscore the potential of pairing symptoms and biomarkers to more efficiently and accurately detect AD cases at risk of clinical progression. papers.title: Plasma Phosphorylated Tau 217 Percentage by Race and Ethnicity in Preclinical Alzheimer Disease.
papers.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In trials targeting preclinical Alzheimer disease (AD), defined as amyloid pathology without cognitive symptoms, racial and ethnic differences in plasma phosphorylated tau 217 percentage (%p-tau217) may influence screening eligibility.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize racial and ethnic differences in %p-tau217 and determine whether associations between %p-tau217, cognition, and amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) differ across groups.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a cross-sectional analysis of AHEAD 3-45 screening participants conducted from July 2020 to October 2024 at 106 sites across 4 world regions. Adults aged 55 to 80 years with %p-tau217 measured before medical and cognitive exclusions (N = 15 612) were included.
EXPOSURES: Self-reported race (Asian, Black, and White) and ethnicity (Hispanic and non-Hispanic) and apolipoprotein E ε4 (APOE ε4) carrier status.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: %p-tau217 levels and associations of %p-tau217 with Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite 5 (PACC5) score and amyloid PET were evaluated across racial and ethnic groups using multivariable linear regression.
RESULTS: Among 15 612 participants, the mean (SD) age was 68.4 (6.2) years; 9941 (63.7%) were female and 5755 (36.9%) were APOE ε4 carriers. %p-tau217 levels were lower among Asian, Black, and Hispanic participants than among White and non-Hispanic participants. APOE ε4 status was associated with higher %p-tau217 across all groups. The association between APOE ε4 status and %p-tau217 differed by race (APOE ε4 × race: F2,14 973 = 10.06; P < .001) and ethnicity (APOE ε4 × ethnicity: β, 0.042; 95% CI, 0.017 to 0.067; P = .005) (Asian: β, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.02 to 0.08; P = .01; Black: β, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.03 to 0.08; P = .002; Hispanic: β, 0.04; 95% CI, 0.02 to 0.07; P = .005). The %p-tau217-PACC5 association showed no pairwise differences across racial groups but differed by ethnicity (β, -0.53; 95% CI, -0.85 to -0.21; P = .008) and APOE ε4 × ethnicity (β, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.26 to 1.30; P = .02). The %p-tau217-PET association showed no significant pairwise differences across racial groups but differed by ethnicity (β, -6.30; 95% CI, -9.10 to -3.51; P < .001) and APOE ε4 × ethnicity (β, 7.12; 95% CI, 2.52 to 11.73; P = .01).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cross-sectional study, plasma %p-tau217 varied across racial and ethnic groups. Consistent %p-tau217-PACC5 score and %p-tau217-PET associations across racial groups support plasma-based screening before PET confirmation, while ethnicity-related findings warrant further investigation.

papers.title: Global Incidence of All-Cause Dementia: A Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Global dementia incidence estimates are limited by underrepresentation of low- and middle-income countries and heterogeneous analytic methods. Due to these limitations, true understanding of the global dementia landscape remains incomplete.
OBJECTIVE: To identify dementia incidence rates by age and sex in various regions worldwide (high-income countries and low- and middle-income countries) where data on clinically based dementia diagnoses were available.
DATA SOURCES: Retrospective community-based cohorts from the Cohort Studies of Memory in an International Consortium (COSMIC); baseline recruitment commenced between January 1990 and December 2011 and follow-up data were collected through the end of 2021. Data were analyzed from June 2024 to June 2025.
STUDY SELECTION: Eligible studies included longitudinal COSMIC cohort studies with a clinically based diagnosis of dementia. Individual participant-level data from 22 population-based longitudinal cohorts (N = 38 418) spanning 18 countries or territories across 6 continents were included.
DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Data extraction and assessment of study quality and validity were conducted according to Meta-Analyses of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (MOOSE) guidelines. Individual participant-level data were meta-analyzed in a 2-step process using random intercepts for country and study at the global and regional levels and by country income level.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: For each study with a clinically based diagnosis, incidence rates for all-cause dementia were calculated and a 2-step meta-analysis was conducted. Using a person-years at risk framework with inverse-probability censoring weights and Poisson models, age- and sex-specific incidence were estimated and then standardized to the 2023 global age-sex population structure.
RESULTS: Across 287 632 person-years at risk, 3001 participants developed dementia. Age- and sex-standardized incidence was 9.7 (95% CI, 7.89-11.97) per 1000 person-years at risk. Age-standardized incidence was higher in women than men (10.6; 95% CI, 8.61-13.11 vs 8.6; 95% CI, 6.94-10.72). Standardized incidence was higher in low- and middle-income countries (13.6; 95% CI, 9.67-19.24) than in high-income countries (8.3; 95% CI, 6.57-10.54). Applying age- and sex-specific rates to the projected 2050 population yielded a projected 24.7 million new cases, assuming constant incidence over time.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The harmonized estimates presented in this study provide a comparable benchmark for global dementia incidence and inform planning for prevention, diagnosis, and memory-care services, particularly in underrepresented low- and middle-income country settings.

papers.title: Plasma p-tau217 and neurodegeneration-related biomarkers predict incident cognitive impairment in obstructive sleep apnea: a prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with cognitive decline, but biomarkers for identifying cognitively unimpaired patients at increased future risk remain limited. We evaluated the prognostic value of plasma biomarkers associated with neuroaxonal injury and Alzheimer's disease-related biology in OSA.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 286 cognitively unimpaired adults with polysomnography-confirmed OSA underwent baseline measurement of plasma NfL, GFAP, p-tau181, p-tau217, Aβ42, and Aβ40 and were followed for incident cognitive impairment. Cox regression, predictive performance analyses, and linear mixed-effects models were used.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 4.18 years, 68 participants (23.78%) developed incident cognitive impairment. In fully adjusted Cox models, each 1-SD increase in NfL was associated with a 46% higher risk of incident cognitive impairment (HR = 1.46, 95% CI 1.17-1.83, P = 0.001), and each 1-SD increase in p-tau217 was associated with a 58% higher risk (HR = 1.58, 95% CI 1.25-2.00, P < 0.001). When modeled jointly, both NfL (HR = 1.34, 95% CI 1.06-1.69, P = 0.014) and p-tau217 (HR = 1.47, 95% CI 1.14-1.89, P = 0.003) remained associated with incident cognitive impairment. In longitudinal analyses, higher baseline NfL and p-tau217 were also associated with faster annual declines in MoCA scores when modeled jointly (NfL × time: β = -0.10, 95% CI - 0.18 to - 0.02, P = 0.014; p-tau217 × time: β = -0.16, 95% CI - 0.25 to - 0.07, P = 0.001). Adding both biomarkers to the clinical model increased the C-index from 0.72 to 0.81 and the 4-year time-dependent AUC to 0.81; the optimism-corrected C-index was 0.79.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher plasma NfL and p-tau217 levels were independently associated with incident cognitive impairment and faster longitudinal cognitive decline in cognitively unimpaired patients with OSA.

papers.title: PPARγ Signaling in the Central Nervous System: A Review of the Implications in Synaptic Plasticity, Neuroinflammatory and Neoplastic Processes.
papers.abstract: Peroxisome proliferator activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) is a ligand activated nuclear receptor traditionally associated with lipid and glucose metabolism. Emerging evidence, however, identifies PPARγ as a central immunometabolic regulator in the central nervous system (CNS), coordinating mitochondrial function, neuroinflammation, synaptic plasticity, and neurovascular integrity. Beyond its classical metabolic actions, PPARγ regulates microglial activation, astrocytic inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial biogenesis, thereby influencing neuronal resilience and circuit stability. This narrative review synthesizes knowledge of PPARγ structure, activation, CNS distribution, endogenous ligands, and synthetic agonists, including thiazolidinediones and selective modulators. We highlight how PPARγ controls transcriptional programs related to energy homeostasis, inflammatory signaling, including NF κB dependent pathways, and blood brain barrier function. Attention is devoted to synaptic remodeling and plasticity, positioning PPARγ as a molecular bridge between metabolic state and neuronal adaptability. We propose that PPARγ signaling dysregulation represents a convergent mechanism in neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and adrenoleukodystrophy; psychiatric conditions, such as depression and anxiety; and neurooncological processes. Integrating evidence across these conditions supports PPARγ as a master regulator of neuroimmune metabolic coupling in the brain. Finally, we discuss translational challenges and opportunities, including brain penetrant, functionally selective ligands, clarification of cell type specific signaling, and expansion of rigorous clinical trials. Integrating mechanistic, preclinical, and clinical trial evidence, this review critically examines the therapeutic potential of PPARγ across neurodegenerative, psychiatric, and neurooncological CNS conditions, while identifying priorities for future therapeutic development in diverse brain disorders.

papers.title: Multiplexed impedimetric zinc oxide nanorods-modified aptasensor on carbon ink-inscribed paper electrodes for the specific and sensitive co-detection of Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD), represent a growing health burden, while early diagnosis remains challenging because established diagnostic approaches, including cerebrospinal fluid analysis and neuroimaging, are invasive, expensive, and unsuitable for decentralized point-of-care testing. Recent progress in electrochemical and paper-based biosensors has enabled low-cost, portable, and multiplexed biomarker analysis. However, their clinical translation remains limited by low biomarker concentrations, matrix interference, nonspecific adsorption, sensor-to-sensor variability, storage stability, and the need for validation using clinical samples. Herein, a paper-based multiplex electrochemical aptasensor was developed for simultaneous impedimetric detection of amyloid beta-42 (Aβ-42) and alpha synuclein-60 (αS-60), biomarkers associated with AD and PD, respectively. The device comprised screen-printed carbon and silver electrodes on a cellulose substrate, two independently functionalized working electrodes, zinc oxide nanorods (ZnO-NRs) as electroactive signal-amplification layers, and target-specific DNA aptamers as biorecognition elements. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy was used for label-free measurement of target-induced changes in charge-transfer resistance. The sensor exhibited a linear response from 0.1 ng/mL to 10 µg/mL for both biomarkers, with limits of detection of 4.41 ng/mL for Aβ-42 and 2.62 ng/mL for αS-60. The platform further detected both analytes in artificial cerebrospinal fluid and artificial saliva, demonstrating that the paper-based sensing interface remains responsive in physiologically mimicked matrices. Overall, this study provides a low-cost, disposable, label-free, and multiplexed proof-of-concept platform for simultaneous AD- and PD-associated biomarker detection. Although the system demonstrates promising performance in artificial matrices, further optimization of sensitivity, surface immobilization, antifouling behaviour, long-term storage, and validation using real clinical saliva and CSF samples will be required before practical diagnostic deployment.

papers.title: CRISPR/Cas9-based nanodelivery systems for precision gene editing in neuroinflammation.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neuroinflammation is a characteristic feature of many neurological diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Uncontrolled activation of microglia and astrocytes results in the production of proinflammatory mediators that contribute to neuronal dysfunction and degeneration.
PURPOSE: CRISPR/Cas9 genome-editing technology provides highly precise targeting of genes involved in these pathways, enabling the deletion, correction, or modulation of disease-associated genetic alterations. Nonetheless, effective delivery of CRISPR components to the central nervous system (CNS) remains a major challenge because of protective barriers such as the blood-brain barrier (BBB), as well as concerns regarding genomic instability and immunogenicity.
METHODS: Nanotechnology-guided delivery platforms, such as lipid nanoparticles, liposomes, dendrimers and polymeric carriers, have been developed as promising strategies to address these challenges. These nanosystems can improve biodistribution, pharmacokinetic behavior, and cellular uptake, while potentially reducing off-target effects and systemic toxicity.
RESULTS: The preclinical studies demonstrate successful modulation of key neuroinflammatory targets, including the NLRP3 inflammasome, triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2), Janus kinase (JAK) signaling, and the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway, with potential therapeutic relevance to neurodegenerative diseases. In addition, novel techniques, such as mitochondrial base editing, prime editing, and epigenetic modulation, expand the scope of CRISPR-mediated therapeutic strategies. Although outcomes from animal models are promising, translation to the clinical setting requires careful consideration of safety, ethical concerns, and long-term efficacy.
CONCLUSIONS: This review highlights the potential of integrating CRISPR/Cas9 with nanodelivery systems to advance precision medicine for neuroinflammatory disorders, while emphasizing their potential for therapeutic applications in complex CNS conditions. Ongoing studies aimed at optimizing delivery and reducing off-target effects will be essential for advancing these approaches toward clinical practice.

papers.title: Psychological impact of the use of blood-based biomarkers for mild cognitive impairment in primary care.
papers.abstract: BackgroundBlood-based biomarker testing in primary care could contribute to the early diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease. The usefulness of using blood-based biomarker in the primary care has evaluated, but their psychological impact has not been examined.ObjectiveThe primary objective of this study is to investigate the psychological impact of disclosing results to patients and evaluate the changes in confidence of diagnoses by physicians. As a secondary objective, we compare the psychological impact with positron emission tomography.MethodsThis study included adults aged ≥50 years with suspected mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia. In total, 97 were analyzed in this study. All participants underwent blood-based biomarker testing and the results were disclosed by primary care physicians or specialists. Psychological impact was measured using the Impact of Event Scale-Revised 1 week after disclosure. Physician diagnostic confidence, changes in diagnosis and management actions were also recorded.ResultsNineteen participants had negative blood-based biomarker results but positive PET results. The Impact of Event Scale-Revised scores were low after blood-based biomarker disclosure and did not differ by health care provider. Blood-based biomarker results prompted changes in diagnosis in 41.9% of cases. The diagnostic confidence increased after disclosure of the blood-based biomarker. Physicians reported a moderate/strong impact on management in 81.5% of cases after the disclosure of blood-based biomarkers.ConclusionsIn this study, blood-based biomarker result disclosure to patients with mild cognitive impairment had minimal short-term psychological burden and informed clinical decisions. These findings support the integration of blood-based biomarker testing into dementia care.

papers.title: Carbon dot-based nanomaterials in neurodegeneration: addressing neurobiological barriers and targeting challenges.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, represent a major global health challenge due to their progressive nature and limited therapeutic options. One of the primary obstacles to treating these disorders is the blood-brain barrier (BBB), which restricts the delivery of most therapeutic agents into the central nervous system. In recent years, carbon-based nanomaterials, particularly carbon dot (CD) nanostructures, have emerged as promising platforms for neurological applications owing to their ultrasmall size, BBB-crossing ability, and anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties, in addition to tunable surface chemistry, strong photoluminescence, and favorable biocompatibility. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent research developments in the application of CD-based nanomaterials, including carbon nanodots, carbon quantum dots, graphene quantum dots, and carbon polymer dots, for the potential treatment of neurodegenerative diseases. The synthesis strategies and carbonization approaches used to produce these carbon nanomaterials are discussed, along with their physicochemical properties relevant to neurobiological applications, such as particle size, surface functionalization, heteroatom doping, optical properties, and stability in biological environments. Furthermore, the mechanisms by which CD-based nanomaterials can traverse the BBB are examined, including receptor-mediated and adsorptive-mediated transcytosis pathways. In addition, their applications are discussed, with particular focus on their roles in bioimaging, biosensing, inhibition of pathological protein aggregation, antioxidative activity, and targeted drug delivery. Finally, key challenges related to toxicity, biodistribution, large-scale synthesis, and clinical translation are discussed, along with future perspectives for the development of multifunctional theranostic platforms. Overall, use of CD-based nanomaterials represents a promising emerging strategy for overcoming neurobiological barriers and enabling the development of next-generation nanotherapeutics for the management of neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of pyrimidine linked fused thiazole-isoxazole conjugates as dual cholinesterase inhibitors for Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) affects over 55 million individuals worldwide, yet approved pharmacotherapies remain limited to symptomatic relief. Dual inhibition of acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BuChE) offers a validated approach to restoring cholinergic tone. However, structurally differentiated inhibitors with favorable selectivity profiles are critically needed. Here, we report a series of pyrimidine clubbed thiazolo[4,5-c]isoxazole framework that functions as potent dual cholinesterase inhibitors with low-micromolar activity against both AChE and BuChE. Lead compound-1 demonstrated IC50 values of 6.19 ± 0.60 μM (AChE) and 8.64 ± 0.91 μM (BuChE) showing promising performance over the reference donepezil (AChE IC50 = 19.38 ± 0.98 μM, BuChE IC50 = 27.54 ± 1.34 μM). Furthermore, structure-activity relationship analysis identified electron-withdrawing (p-CF3, p-F, o,p-Cl, p-NO2) and electron-donating (-OH) aryl substituents as principal modulators of inhibitory potency. Moreover, molecular docking against human AChE and BuChE crystal structures revealed dual engagement of the catalytic anionic site and peripheral anionic site through hydrogen-bonding and π-π stacking interactions. In silico ADMET profiling confirmed electronic reactivity and drug-likeness of lead compounds. These findings establish pyrimidine-clubbed thiazolo[4,5-c]isoxazole as a mechanistically grounded scaffold with translational potential for next-generation anti-Alzheimer therapeutics.

papers.title: Metal Oxides Catalyze Formation of Dehydroamino Acids by Phosphate β-Elimination Under Physiological Conditions.
papers.abstract: The dehydroamino acids (DHAAs) dehydroalanine and dehydrobutyrine are formed in proteins posttranslationally from serine and threonine, respectively. They contain an electrophilic alkene, which reacts readily with nucleophiles by Michael addition, giving rise to a variety of chemical modifications as well as protein crosslinks. Recent work has shown DHAAs and their modifications to be highly prevalent in protein aggregates isolated from brains of Alzheimer's Disease (AD) patients. As there is no human enzyme known to catalyze the formation of DHAAs, this raised the question of how they are produced. We show here that metal oxides, particularly the iron oxides goethite and hematite, efficiently catalyze the formation of DHAAs in model phosphopeptides in vitro under physiologically relevant conditions. Iron oxides are known to accumulate in the human brain with age, and this deposition is enhanced in neurodegenerative disorders like AD. The DHAA formation by heterogeneous catalysis reported here provides a previously unknown mechanism linking iron deposition to protein crosslinking in AD and potentially other neurodegenerative diseases where iron accumulation and protein aggregation co-occur.

papers.title: A Community's Voice: Community Advisory Boards in ADRD Biomarker Research Among Older Black Women.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) disproportionately affect Black/African American (BAA) women, yet this afflicted population remains underrepresented in ADRD biomarker research. As ADRD blood-based biomarkers become increasingly available, research must prioritize equity and inclusivity to determine their diagnostic specificity in minoritized groups. Community Advisory Boards (CABs) are pivotal in ensuring culturally responsive and community-engaged research. This article outlines the formation, operation, and maintenance of the Black Women: Inflammation and Tau Study (BWITS) CAB, which has played a crucial role in guiding the BWITS Research Team by refining research protocols and safeguarding the cultural contexts of the communities it represents. Motivated by a commitment to the BAA community, we advocate for a transformative shift in ADRD research on minoritized populations, emphasizing the need for CAB input to ensure accountability and the implementation of culturally responsive methods, benefiting both the scientific and target communities.

papers.title: Preliminary evidence for script generation as an efficient, objective measure of everyday function in older adults.
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Mild difficulties performing everyday activities may emerge early in Alzheimer's disease and Alzheimer's disease-related dementias, creating a need for objective, efficient measures sensitive to subtle functional changes. This study investigated a script generation task (SGT), which required individuals to verbally describe the steps needed to complete familiar everyday activities, as a potential method for detecting mild functional difficulties in older adults with or without mild cognitive impairment (MCI). We examined both human-coded features of script generation and automated linguistic features using natural language processing (NLP).
METHODS: 83 community-dwelling older adults (mean age = 73.59 years; 67% female; 55% White; n = 57 cognitively unimpaired on testing [CU]; n = 26 MCI) completed the SGT, requiring them to describe the steps for four everyday tasks: making toast, preparing instant coffee, making a peanut butter and jelly sandwich, and preparing a lunchbox. SGT performance was scored by human coders for total steps, words, and errors and analyzed using NLP measures of pronoun-to-noun ratio, lexical density, and lexical sophistication. Participants also completed a performance-based test of everyday function (Naturalistic Action Test, NAT), self-report questionnaires regarding everyday function, and cognitive tests.  .
RESULTS: After controlling for age, education, and estimated IQ, participants with MCI generated significantly fewer SGT steps than CU participants and used more pronouns relative to nouns, reflecting less specificity in their speech. The ability to generate SGT steps was associated with cognitive tests of episodic memory, and both SGT steps and total words were associated with executive function. Participants who generated more SGT words also completed more steps on the NAT. These associations survived correction for multiple comparisons. By contrast, SGT measures were not significantly associated with self-reported everyday functioning after correction for multiple comparisons.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings provide support for the potential use of the SGT as an objective and efficient measure of mild functional difficulties in older adults. Future work is needed to evaluate the predictive validity of the SGT and to develop automated scoring programs to increase scalability.

papers.title: Diabetes-Associated Cognitive Impairment: Pathophysiology and Emerging Therapies.
papers.abstract: Diabetes-associated cognitive impairment (DACI) is a common yet underrecognized condition, manifesting along a spectrum from mild cognitive impairment to dementia. DACI encompasses patients who develop vascular dementia (VaD) or Alzheimer's disease (AD) with diabetes as a risk factor; however, in certain patients, particularly those lacking clear VaD or AD features, diabetes may act as a primary driver of neurodegeneration. Mechanistically, DACI can be conceptualized as a neurovascular-metabolic disorder characterized by disruption of the neurovascular unit, impaired cerebral glucose metabolism, brain insulin resistance, and chronic neuroinflammation, contributing to small vessel disease, regional brain atrophy, and accelerated brain aging. In this narrative review, we synthesize current evidence on the clinical and imaging features of DACI, outline key mechanistic pathways linking diabetes to neurodegeneration, and discuss emerging therapeutic strategies, including GLP-1 receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors, with potential neuroprotective effects. Greater recognition of DACI as a neurovascular-metabolic entity may facilitate earlier identification, inform biomarker development, and guide future trials aimed at preserving cognitive function in individuals with diabetes.

papers.title: Exploratory bone-brain transcriptomic associations and an ODE-based digital-twin framework for fracture healing.
papers.abstract: Fracture healing is generally viewed as a local tissue-regeneration process, although skeletal injury can also elicit systemic immune, vascular, and neural responses. We used a stratified analytical strategy combining reanalysis of public transcriptomic datasets, descriptive single-nucleus profiling, and an ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based simulation of fracture healing to examine possible associations between adverse bone phenotypes and Alzheimer disease. In the primary random-effects meta-analysis of three retained human bone-related binary cohorts, 72 prespecified panel genes were measured in all three cohorts; BMP10 and ANGPT1 had the smallest adjusted P values. In the separate GSE48350 whole-brain dataset, 6 of 84 mapped target genes had nominal P < 0.05. Descriptive single-nucleus RNA-sequencing analysis of GSE138852 showed within-dataset, cell-type-specific expression patterns across annotated neural cell populations. The eight-state ODE prototype, built on prespecified assumptions, generated fracture-healing trajectories and scenario-dependent model outputs. Tissue-expression and genetic analyses provided additional exploratory context for the selected genes. These analyses define a hypothesis-generating framework for studying skeletal-neural associations after fracture.

papers.title: Field-assisted interfacial passivation: Microwave-enhanced EGCG remodeling of amyloid-β42 aggregates.
papers.abstract: Amyloid misfolding and self-assembly are central pathological events of Alzheimer's disease and related proteinopathies. Although soluble oligomers are widely considered as the primary toxic species, how therapeutic modulators alter toxicity-relevant aggregate surfaces remains poorly understood. Here, we combine cell viability assays, thioflavin T (ThT) aggregation kinetics, circular dichroism (CD), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate how microwave-assisted Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) remodels Aβ42 aggregates. We show that microwave exposure markedly enhanced EGCG-mediated cytoprotection in BV2 microglial cells while concurrently suppressing the formation of canonical ThT-responsive amyloid species. MD simulations revealed that oscillating electric fields promote a constrained, interface-selective remodeling of protofibrillar-like aggregates rather than catastrophic depolymerization. In the initial trajectory pair, field assistance redistributed EGCG contacts across more surface residues, accompanied by reduced overall and hydrophobic protein-only solvent-accessible surface area. At a key hydrophobic interface identified by contact-occupancy analysis, the combined treatment decreased local water density and solvent accessibility, indicating reduced local hydration. We define this collective surface state- characterized by expanded EGCG coverage, reduced hydrophobic exposure, and diminished solvent accessibility - as interfacial passivation. Moreover, simulation analysis revealed that the field-assisted EGCG adsorption state remains stable for at least 500 ns after field removal, suggesting that the electric field facilitates formation of a kinetically stable surface-bound configuration. Together, these findings support field-assisted interfacial passivation as a possible mechanism for amyloid modulation and suggest that passivating toxicity-relevant aggregate surfaces, rather than achieving complete depolymerization, may represent a promising therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Perfusion quality does not necessarily predict ultrastructural preservation after hyperosmotic brain perfusion.
papers.abstract: Perfusion fixation is widely used in neuroscience to prepare mammalian brain tissue for histological and ultrastructural analysis. Perfusion protocols are commonly assessed using macroscopic indicators such as gross appearance and neuroimaging, which assess the extent to which perfusate has been distributed throughout the brain. There is a critical need to determine to what extent these metrics can accurately predict high-quality ultrastructural preservation, particularly as new perfusion protocols are developed for connectomics. In this technical report, we describe evidence that these two measures can be decoupled by the addition of dehydrating agents to the perfusate solution. In three human brain donors and one canine brain donor perfused with a fixative solution containing 10% mannitol and 10% polyethylene glycol 35 kDa, macroscopic and radiological indicators of perfusion quality appeared adequate or favorable. However, electron microscopy revealed expanded extracellular space, shrunken cellular processes, and distorted cell membranes, consistent with an osmotic shock artifact resulting from severe hyperosmotic dehydration. Similar ultrastructural artifacts were observed in a canine brain donor perfused with 20% mannitol in 20% neutral buffered formalin without PEG. We compare these ultrastructural findings with findings from previously reported cases perfused with standard neutral buffered formalin without osmotic additives. These findings illustrate a risk of optimizing brain perfusion protocols designed to preserve neural circuitry based on macroscopic or radiological perfusion quality metrics alone, since these metrics can be satisfied while the ultrastructure is severely compromised.

papers.title: ATRI LIMS: a cloud-native open-source laboratory information management system for biomarker-driven Alzheimer's disease clinical trials.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This article summarizes the architecture, design principles, and implementation strategy of the ATRI Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS), a cloud‑native, open‑source platform supporting biomarker‑driven Alzheimer's disease (AD) clinical research. The system addresses challenges associated with managing large‑scale, multimodal biomarker, and biobanking data across multisite studies.
METHODS: The ATRI LIMS employs a Model-View-Controller architecture implemented in Django, with Single‑Page Application interfaces built in ReactJS. A hybrid database model integrates a normalized core schema with study‑specific extensions. Deployment on Amazon Web Services incorporates multifactor authentication, encryption, and a web application firewall. Regulatory support is provided through audit trails and electronic signatures. Development relied on collaboration between informatics engineers and laboratory personnel, with user acceptance testing guiding workflow and interface refinement.
RESULTS: As of February 2026, the ATRI LIMS supports seven clinical trials and observational studies and manages more than 1.2 million biospecimens. The platform synchronizes biospecimen metadata and assay outputs with clinical datasets, improves operational efficiency through automated workflows and quality control, and facilitates compliant sample sharing for secondary research. AI‑assisted development accelerated feature delivery while maintaining code quality.
DISCUSSION: The ATRI LIMS offers a scalable, adaptable informatics framework for biomarker‑intensive AD research. Its modular design, cloud‑native architecture, and comprehensive data management capabilities support accurate specimen tracking and coordinated data integration. An open-source release is planned to enable adoption and adaptation by other research programs.
CONCLUSIONS: The ATRI LIMS enhances informatics infrastructure for modern AD research by enabling scalable, efficient, and compliant biomarker and biospecimen workflow management.

papers.title: Cerebral Hemodynamic Changes in Older Adults With Cognitive Complaints According to the Presence of Peripheral Artery Disease.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: As a systemic expression of atherosclerosis, peripheral artery disease (PAD) has the potential to alter cerebral hemodynamics in elderly individuals presenting with cognitive concerns. However, how PAD status shapes the longitudinal trajectory of cerebral hemodynamics has not been well characterized.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center longitudinal observational study enrolling 132 participants (21 controls, 39 mild cognitive impairment, 72 mild Alzheimer's disease). All participants underwent transcranial Doppler (TCD) ultrasonography, ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurement, brain MRI, and cognitive assessments at baseline and follow-up (~13.45 months). PAD was defined as ABI < 0.90. Bilateral mean flow velocity (MFV), pulsatility index (PI), and resistance index (RI) of the middle cerebral artery (MCA) were tracked longitudinally across both time points.
RESULTS: PAD was identified in 13 participants (9.8%). Baseline TCD parameters, vascular risk factors, white matter lesions on brain MRI, and cognitive measures were comparable between groups. At follow-up, the PAD group showed significantly higher MCA MFV after age adjustment (left p < 0.001; right p = 0.005). MFV increased in the PAD group (left +16.45 cm/s) but decreased in the non-PAD group (left -3.37 cm/s), with a significant between-group difference. PI and RI did not change in either group. Cognitive and functional outcomes were similar across groups throughout the study.
CONCLUSION: These findings identify PAD as a condition associated with progressive MCA MFV elevation in the context of preserved cognition, implying that subclinical cerebrovascular changes are detectable by TCD before overt clinical worsening. Future research involving larger cohorts and extended follow-up is required to determine whether such hemodynamic changes forecast eventual cognitive deterioration.

papers.title: The Gut-Brain Axis and Neurodegenerative Diseases: From Mechanistic Pathways to Therapeutic Interventions.
papers.abstract: As the global population ages, the incidence of neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs) has increased. Neurodegenerative diseases have complex pathogenesis and currently lack fundamental treatment methods. The gut-brain axis (GBA) participates in the pathogenesis of NDDs through bidirectional communication between the gut microbiota and the central nervous system (CNS). This review systematically introduces the pathogenic characteristics of representative NDDs such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and multiple sclerosis (MS), as well as the association mechanisms between these diseases and GBA. The pathogenic characteristics of NDDs are closely related to changes in the composition of the gut microbiota and differences in gut microbiota metabolites (such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), neurotransmitters, tryptophan metabolites, etc.). These changes influence the CNS through multiple pathways, including neuroendocrine, vagus nerve, and immune regulation, ultimately contributing to the onset and progression of the diseases. Furthermore, we have collected and summarized preclinical and clinical evidence from recent years regarding therapeutic interventions based on the GBA mechanism, including probiotics, prebiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). Nevertheless, major knowledge gaps remain, particularly regarding causality between gut microbiota changes and NDDs, the underlying molecular mechanisms, and the clinical efficacy of GBA-targeted therapies. This article aims to review the mechanisms of the interaction between the gut microbiota and the brain in neurodegenerative diseases, and based on the existing experimental evidence, provide theoretical basis and future development directions for future prevention and treatment strategies targeting GBA.
