papers.title: Characterizing hippocampal activation during pattern separation with multi-echo fMRI in cognitively normal older adults.
papers.abstract: Hippocampal hyperactivity, detected with mnemonic similarity task (MST) fMRI, is both a promising marker of risk and a probable driver of degeneration in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, implementation of such fMRI in interventional research is limited by long scan times and the absence of a framework for identifying prospective participants with hyperactivity who could be targeted with therapeutic approaches aimed at reducing this activity. We used multi-echo fMRI during the MST, an episodic memory task previously shown to engage hippocampal subfields CA3 and dentate gyrus (DG), to characterize activity profiles in 33 cognitively normal older adults. We compared MST-related CA3 and DG activation and behavioural performance across subsets of eight task runs. Behavioural and activation effects were equivalent for the first set of four runs (Runs-A) and the second set (Runs-B), suggesting that robust data can be obtained with four runs. Left and right CA3 + DG activation did not differ. We provide an exemplar framework for the derivation of a threshold for single-participant classification of elevated hippocampal activation as an indicator of AD risk in cognitively normal older individuals. Scalable (~22 min) multi-echo MST fMRI robustly captures hippocampal activation and provides a framework for individual-level characterization of hippocampal function in cognitively normal older adults. This enables individualized detection of elevated hippocampal activation as a modifiable risk factor and may guide enrolment into prevention trials targeting preclinical AD.

papers.title: Integrative Transcriptomic and Interactome Analyses Prioritize Candidate Genes for Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder characterized by complex molecular alterations and diverse cognitive, behavioral, and neuropsychiatric manifestations. Although transcriptomic studies have identified several pathways associated with AD, the integration of molecular signatures with disease-related phenotype annotations and pathological aging remains incompletely understood. Therefore, this study aimed to integrate transcriptomic profiling, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, pathological aging assessment, and curated clinical phenotype annotations to prioritize candidate molecular signatures associated with AD. Differential expression analyses and network-based approaches were applied to publicly available transcriptomic datasets derived from distinct brain regions. Candidate genes and pathways were prioritized through interactome reconstruction, functional enrichment analyses, cluster-based analyses, and independent validation in an external dataset. In addition, transcriptomic signatures were integrated with curated clinical phenotype annotations using a knowledge-based gene overlap strategy. The analysis identified molecular signatures associated with neuroinflammatory signaling, synaptic dysfunction, endocytosis, and pathological aging. Pathways related to MAPK, PI3K/Akt, NF-κB, and TGF-β1 signaling emerged as candidate dysregulated pathways in AD. Comparative analyses of physiological aging and the AD aging comparison enabled the prioritization of candidate genes potentially more closely associated with the AD condition than with aging alone, including FOS and TAB2. Independent validation reinforced the reproducibility of several prioritized genes, including GFAP, CXCR4, CCL2, HSPA1A, FCGR2A, TLR2, CD44, TLR4, FOS, TAB2, CDC42, and SH3GL2. Integration with curated clinical phenotype annotations suggested partially overlapping molecular signatures across neuropsychiatric and cognitive phenotype annotations in AD. Together, these findings demonstrate the utility of integrative bioinformatics approaches for prioritizing candidate genes, pathways, and molecular signatures associated with AD. This systems-level framework may contribute to future mechanistic studies aimed at understanding the molecular heterogeneity of AD and its associated phenotypic complexity.

papers.title: Glyceryl tribenzoate, a flavoring agent, stimulates hippocampal plasticity and protects memory via PPARα.
papers.abstract: Glyceryl tribenzoate (GTB) or tribenzoin is a flavoring agent with characteristic anti-microbial property. We have already delineated GTB's immunomodulatory role via the enrichment of regulatory T cells in mouse models of multiple sclerosis and anti-neuroinflammatory role via the reduction of glial activation in a monkey model of Parkinson's disease and a mouse model of Huntington's disease. However, its role has never been explored in Alzheimer's disease (AD), the most common neurodegenerative disorder in human. This study underlines the importance of GTB in promoting the growth and function of hippocampal neurons via upregulation of plasticity-associated genes, enrichment of dendritic spines and stimulation of inotropic calcium influx. Accordingly, oral GTB improved hippocampal plasticity and protected memory and learning in 5xFAD mice. Similarly, GTB treatment also reduced cerebral plaque load and increased the life span of aged 5xFAD mice. Interestingly, we observed that peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα), a nuclear hormone receptor, served as a receptor of GTB. Consequently, GTB was shown to improve hippocampal plasticity and increase cognitive functions in 5xFAD, but not 5xFAD/Ppara-null, mice, indicating an important role of PPARα in GTB-mediated neuroprotection. These results suggest that oral GTB may have therapeutic importance for improving hippocampal functions in AD patients.

papers.title: Beyond the brain-centric view: A systems physiology framework for exercise-induced neuroprotection in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is regarded as a multifactorial disease that combines central pathological changes and peripheral organ dysfunction. Its core features include Aβ protein deposition, tau protein pathology, synaptic dysfunction, and neuroinflammation. Exercise has been proven to be one of the most effective non-pharmacological intervention measures. However, its mechanism of action in AD has not been fully elucidated from the traditional brain-centered research perspective. Moreover, most existing studies focus on isolated organ systems or a single signaling pathway, failing to fully reflect the overall peripheral-cerebral physiological interaction mechanism required for neuroprotective effects of exercise. This article provides a structured narrative synthesis of current evidence regarding how exercise may influence AD-related pathological processes through multiple peripheral organ systems. It clarifies the communication mechanisms between these systems and the central nervous system through endocrine, immune, metabolic, neural, and vascular pathways. The study shows that exercise functions by coordinating the regulation of peripheral physiological functions, rather than relying on a single target mechanism. Exercise can regulate multiple signaling pathways such as muscle-brain, gut-brain, liver-brain, adipose-brain, bone-brain, and immune-brain, improving overall metabolic flexibility, inflammation regulation, vascular function, and neuroimmune homeostasis; these peripheral adaptive changes further act on the central nervous system, regulating blood-brain barrier(BBB) integrity, microglial cell activity, neuronal energy metabolism, neurovascular coupling, and synaptic plasticity. In summary, the neuroprotective effect induced by exercise stems from the integration of multiple systems' physiology, rather than isolated molecular signal transduction. This review synthesizes current evidence on exercise-induced peripheral-central interactions in AD from a systems physiology perspective, highlighting the significance of integrating peripheral biomarkers, multi-organ interactions, and central outcomes. It provides a theoretical framework for future personalized and mechanism-oriented exercise intervention studies.

papers.title: Baseline and longitudinal trajectories of peak expiratory flow in relation to incident cognitive impairment among older adults: Evidence from CHARLS.
papers.abstract: BackgroundPrevious studies, including CHARLS analyses, have linked lower peak expiratory flow (PEF) with cognitive decline. Evidence regarding incident score-based cognitive impairment, longitudinal PEF patterns, and incremental prediction remains limited.ObjectiveTo examine associations of baseline PEF and exploratory PEF trajectories with incident score-based cognitive impairment and evaluate the incremental predictive value of PEF.MethodsThe primary analysis included 2604 CHARLS participants aged ≥60 years without score-based cognitive impairment at baseline. Cognitive impairment was defined as a global cognitive score ≥1 SD below the wave- and age-specific mean and was not a clinical diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment or dementia. Cox models, sensitivity analyses, prediction analyses, and exploratory trajectory modeling were performed.ResultsOver a median follow-up of 9.0 years, 636 participants developed score-based cognitive impairment. Each 1-SD increase in PEF was associated with lower risk in fully adjusted models (HR = 0.801, 95% CI 0.728-0.880) and after adjustment for baseline cognition (HR = 0.846, 95% CI 0.768-0.930). Nine-year cumulative incidence decreased from 35.6% to 16.6% across PEF quartiles. Adding PEF modestly improved 9-year AUC (ΔAUC = 0.011, p = 0.042). In the exploratory trajectory analysis, the moderate PEF group was not significantly associated with risk versus the high group (HR = 1.294, 95% CI 0.860-1.948), whereas the low PEF group had higher risk (HR = 1.817, 95% CI 1.172-2.817), with no clear graded pattern.ConclusionsLower baseline PEF was associated with wave-specific score-based cognitive impairment, but not under stricter definitions requiring subsequent confirmation with wave-specific or fixed thresholds. PEF trajectories were exploratory, and incremental predictive value was limited.

papers.title: Single-cell gene networks nominate IKZF1 as an Alzheimer's disease microglial regulator.
papers.abstract: BackgroundMicroglia drive neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet no approved therapy targets this compartment. Human genome-wide association studies consistently implicate innate immune loci in AD risk, establishing microglial transcriptional programs as therapeutically relevant but pharmacologically underexploited targets.ObjectiveWe sought to identify transcription factors (TFs) governing microglial state transitions computationally and to nominate structurally tractable drug repurposing candidates.MethodsWe applied trajectory inference (PAGA), pseudobulk DESeq2, pySCENIC gene regulatory network (GRN) inference, CellChat, and virtual screening of 1962 approved compounds to 236,002 microglial nuclei from 84 donors (SEA-AD atlas).ResultsIKZF1 was the sole target TF retained under cisTarget v10 motif constraints, with peak regulon activity in LateAD-DAM (pseudotime ρ = + 0.309) and replication in an independent bulk cohort (GSE95587; adjusted p = 0.004). CellChat identified SLIT2→ROBO2 from multiple neuron subtypes (predominantly inhibitory interneurons) as the top predicted pathway to microglia. Tafamidis (→IRF8) and diflunisal (→PPARG) were top virtual screening hits; all evaluated compounds failed the pre-specified selectivity threshold.ConclusionsIKZF1 is prioritized as a candidate late-disease microglial TF, supported by six convergent evidence dimensions including independent bulk replication. Tafamidis and diflunisal are low-confidence repurposing hypotheses requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: Noise or clearance? Reframing plasma amyloid-β variability in Alzheimer's disease as a measurable clearance signal.
papers.abstract: Plasma biomarkers, and the amyloid-β 42/40 ratio in particular, are increasingly used to stage Alzheimer's disease and to stratify and monitor clinical trials, on the tacit assumption that a single measurement reflects a stable, steady-state level of pathology. A recent micro-longitudinal study that sampled plasma weekly for five weeks in people with Alzheimer's disease challenged that assumption, reporting that most participants varied by more than half in the amyloid-β 42/40 ratio over that short window. The reflexive response is to treat such movement as measurement noise to be averaged away. Here I argue that a meaningful part of it is unlikely to be noise. In healthy adults the same ratio is among the most stable plasma analytes, so instability concentrated in disease is difficult to attribute to the assay alone. Brain-to-blood clearance of amyloid-β is itself dynamic over days, rising with sleep and falling with fragmentation, apnoea, poor cerebral perfusion, autonomic dysregulation, and sedating or anticholinergic drugs. An instantaneous plasma value therefore partly reports the clearance state of the preceding night. This clearance account is kept distinct from analytical and pre-analytical variance, and from oligomeric amyloid-β dynamics, which are considered separately. The practical problem is not the variance itself but that we measure the molecule without measuring the physiological state that moves it. I propose that an inexpensive, repeatable, bedside index of that state, illustrated here with the Systemic BenBrik Geriatric Score, could be recorded alongside each plasma draw and modelled as a covariate, converting nuisance variance into interpretable signal. The prediction is falsifiable, and a validation design is outlined. This is a hypothesis, not a validated result; the illustrative index used here, the Systemic BenBrik Geriatric Score, is not a validated measure.

papers.title: Interaction of physical fitness and resting state functional connectivity on global cognitive function in older adults with mild cognitive impairment.
papers.abstract: BackgroundMild cognitive impairment (MCI) represents a prodromal stage of Alzheimer's disease. Physical fitness, including cardiorespiratory fitness and muscular strength, is associated with cognitive function in older adults. Resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) is also linked to cognitive function; however, whether physical fitness modifies the association between rsFC and cognitive function remains unclear.ObjectiveTo examine associations of cardiorespiratory fitness and muscular strength with rsFC and their interaction on global cognitive function in older adults with MCI.MethodsA cross-sectional study of 95 older adults with MCI. Cardiorespiratory fitness was estimated by the 400-m walk; muscular strength was indexed using grip strength measured by hand dynamometer. Global cognitive function was indexed by the 13-item Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive (ADAS-Cog-13). Using the Yeo 7-network atlas, we computed rsFC within and between seven canonical networks. Significant rsFC-fitness associations were entered into moderation analyses (X = rsFC, Y = ADAS-Cog-13) with cardiorespiratory fitness or grip strength as moderator, adjusted for covariates. Simple slopes were examined at ±1 SD from the mean of moderator.ResultsParticipants had a mean age of 73.49 years, and 53.7% were female. Cardiorespiratory fitness interacted with rsFC in relation to ADAS-Cog-13, whereas grip strength did not. Specifically, greater limbic-visual (standardized b = -0.22, p = 0.009), limbic-somatomotor (b = -0.20, p = 0.049), and limbic-ventral attention (b = -0.19, p = 0.020) rsFC were associated with better global cognitive function among individuals with higher cardiorespiratory fitness.ConclusionsHigher between-network rsFC is generally associated with worse cognitive function. Thus, higher cardiorespiratory fitness may attenuate the negative association between higher between-network rsFC and global cognitive function in MCI.

papers.title: High-intensity transcranial alternating current stimulation improves sleep quality in patients with mild Alzheimer's disease: Findings from the TRANSFORM-AD study.
papers.abstract: BackgroundHigh-intensity transcranial alternating current stimulation (Hi-tACS) has shown beneficial effects on cognitive function in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, data on the effects of hi-tACS on sleep quality and emotional state in patients with AD are still limited.ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the influences of hi-tACS on sleep quality and emotional state in AD.MethodsThe TRANSFORM-AD study was a double-blind, randomized-controlled trial that enrolled individuals with mild AD. Participants were randomized to receive hi-tACS group or sham stimulation group, and underwent 30 one-hour sessions of either 40 Hz tACS or sham stimulation over consecutive 15 consecutive days. Pittsburgh sleep quality index (PSQI), Hamilton anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA), Hamilton depression Rating Scale (HAMD) and Quality of life in Alzheimer's Disease scale (QOL-AD) were evaluated at baseline, and the end of the intervention.ResultsAmong 43 participants with complete baseline and post-intervention assessments, Hi-tACS reduced post-intervention PSQI scores compared with sham after adjustment for baseline PSQI (adjusted mean difference, -2.34 points; 95% CI, -3.63 to -1.05; p < 0.001). Baseline-adjusted effects for HAMA (-1.43; 95% CI, -2.89 to 0.02), HAMD (0.44; 95% CI, -1.28 to 2.15), and QOL-AD (2.07; 95% CI, -1.57 to 5.70) were imprecise and included the null.ConclusionHi-tACS improved subjective sleep quality in patients with mild AD. The present secondary analysis did not provide conclusive evidence of effects on anxiety, depression, or quality of life; these exploratory outcomes require confirmation in larger, adequately powered trials.Trial registration:ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03920826.

papers.title: Prevalence and impact of cerebral small vessel lesions in mild cognitive impairment and mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease patients in memory clinic: Preparation for anti-amyloid therapy in Thailand.
papers.abstract: BackgroundAlzheimer's disease (AD) raises global concern with its impact on daily living. Anti-amyloid therapy (AAT) are specific treatments used in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and mild dementia stage of AD (mild AD). Severe cerebral small vessel disease (SVD) lesions such as microbleeds, superficial siderosis, lacunes, white matter hyperintensities are listed as exclusions criteria for AAT. In Thailand, there is no prevalence study of SVD lesions specifically in these patient groups.ObjectiveThe purpose of this study is to report the prevalence of SVD burdens which are excluded in AAT, in MCI and mild AD patients in Thailand.MethodsThe study was carried out at Memory Clinic in King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital. Patients with amnestic MCI and mild AD were diagnosed using clinical criteria, cognitive tests and brain MRI. Visual rating scales were used to evaluate SVD burden based on STRIVE-2 criteria. Baseline characteristics and cognitive tests were retrieved from electronic medical records.ResultsThe study involving 102 patients, 73.5% had MCI, and 26.5% had mild AD. Twenty-one individuals (20.6%) had either more than 4 microbleeds, more than 2 lacunes, or Fazekas score of 3. There was no evidence of superficial siderosis. Individuals without microbleeds had a higher TMSE score (25.4 versus 23.5; p = 0.009).ConclusionsAmong patients with MCI and mild AD, 20.6% met the exclusion criteria for AAT, in part of SVD lesions. These findings provide important information for evaluating the cost-effectiveness of AAT, which become a treatment option for Thai AD patients.

papers.title: Neuroprotective effects of lithium and caffeic acid co-loaded liposomes in diabetes-induced Alzheimer's disease: association with GSK-3β and β-catenin.
papers.abstract:
AIM: To investigate the therapeutic effects of co-loaded lithium (Li) and caffeic acid (CA) liposomes in diabetes-induced Alzheimer's disease rats by improving cognitive dysfunction and attenuating neurodegeneration through the modulation of β-catenin/GSK-3β signaling.
METHODS: Li- and CA-co-loaded liposomes were prepared by the ethanol injection method and characterized. A diabetes-induced Alzheimer's disease model was established in male Wistar rats using a high-fat diet followed by low-dose streptozotocin (35 mg/kg) administered intraperitoneally. Li- and CA-co-loaded liposomes were given via the same route every day for 4 weeks. At the end of the experiment, the animals were sacrificed, and various biochemical and oxidative stress parameters, histopathological assessments, and ELISA analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Dual-drug-loaded Li and CA liposomal treatment significantly improved cognitive function, ameliorated metabolic dysfunction, and reduced oxidative stress by restoring antioxidant enzyme levels. Additionally, liposomes attenuated nitrite, acetylcholinesterase, and amyloid-β levels in diabetes-induced Alzheimer's rats. Histopathological assessment confirmed marked neuroprotective and pancreatic protective effects. Further, at a molecular level, Li and CA liposomal treatment reduced the expression of GSK-3β and increased the expression of β-catenin levels in rats.
CONCLUSION: This study provides the first evidence demonstrating the therapeutic potential of Li- and CA-co-loaded liposomes in attenuating diabetes‑associated cognitive dysfunction.

papers.title: Cerebellar Network Organization in Parkinson's Disease: Functional Connectivity across Motor and Cognitive Circuits.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The cerebellum is increasingly recognized as a key contributor to cognitive reserve and network organization in Parkinson's disease (PD). However, the relationship of cerebello-cortical and cerebello-basal ganglia connectivity with cognitive status and nigrostriatal integrity remains incompletely understood.
METHODS: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data from 172 participants with PD in the Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative were analyzed. Cerebello-basal ganglia and cerebello-cortical connectivity were investigated using region of interest (ROI)-to-ROI and seed-to-voxel approaches. Cerebellar connectivity was examined in relation to cognitive status, age, disease duration, motor severity, dopaminergic medication exposure, and contralateral putaminal striatal binding ratio (SBR).
RESULTS: PD participants demonstrated robust positive cerebello-basal ganglia connectivity, particularly between lobule VI/vermis VI and the pallidum. Greater age was associated with widespread reductions in cerebello-basal ganglia coupling. Longer disease duration was associated with stronger connectivity within cerebellar and basal ganglia circuits, and among cognitively unimpaired participants, stronger lobule V connectivity with temporal regions. After adjustment for contralateral putaminal SBR, cognitively unimpaired participants generally demonstrated greater connectivity between left cerebellar regions and frontal networks, whereas cognitively impaired participants showed greater connectivity from posterior cerebellar and vermal regions, including regions implicated in cognitive processing, to temporal, parahippocampal, occipital, parietal, and somatosensory regions.
CONCLUSIONS: Cerebellar functional connectivity in PD shows region-specific differences across cognitive status rather than uniform network loss with cognitive impairment. These findings support further investigation of cerebellar functional connectivity as a candidate biomarker of cognitive resilience and network adaptation in PD. © 2026 The Author(s). papers.title: Patient and care partner perspectives of a teleneuropsychology intervention: a mixed-methods evaluation.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: While neuropsychological evaluations by telehealth are a valid alternative to face-to-face (FF) visits, teleneuropsychology has not been widely adopted. We explored patient and care partner perspectives on acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, and use of teleneuropsychology to evaluate possible Alzheimer's disease.
METHODS: Using mixed methods, we evaluated patient and care partner's quantitative surveys and qualitative interviews after two neuropsychology modalities: Teleneuropsychology or FF. Surveys included acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility measures, and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology questionnaire. Median scores and interquartile ranges were compared. Interviews focused on implementation outcomes and intention to use. Qualitative analyses identified salient themes, which were integrated with quantitative findings.
RESULTS: Patients and care partners (94 and 93% non-Hispanic white) reported similar positive (median score = 4.0 on a 5-point scale) ratings for Teleneuropsychology and FF. Interviews found that benefits of Teleneuropsychology were support for care partner involvement, minimization of logistical demands, reduced travel burden, and increased comfort within a patient's home. Benefits of FF included increased interpersonal connection, improved communication with the provider, and less stress with technology. Some patients tended to prefer FF, while some care partners tended to prefer Teleneuropsychology.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients and care partners in this homogeneous sample indicated that both modalities were acceptable, appropriate, and feasible. Although quantitative ratings were similar, the "appropriate" choice for a particular patient and care partner dyad seemed to be a personalized consideration of tradeoffs that they navigated together. When Teleneuropsychology is adopted, attention to preferences and feasibility among diverse patients is needed.

papers.title: Nose-to-brain delivery of a novel boronated curcuminoid via cyclodextrins: Biodistribution toward potential BNCT applications in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: This study investigates the selective accumulation of a boronated monocarbonyl curcuminoid (BMAC-9) complexed with β-cyclodextrins in the amyloid-rich brain regions of APP/PS1dE9 transgenic mice, an established model of Alzheimer's disease, compared to C57BL/6 healthy mice. The goal is to develop and evaluate a novel delivery system for the boronated curcuminoid BMAC-9 and to determine whether the resulting boron concentrations in the brain, particularly in the cortex and hippocampus, which are typically enriched in amyloid plaques in patients with Alzheimer's disease, could reach levels potentially suitable for Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT). Physicochemical characterization displayed that BMAC-9 has a logD of 3.45 at both physiological (7.4) and nasal (5.5) pH, suggesting good membrane permeability but poor aqueous solubility. To optimize delivery and facilitate blood-brain barrier (BBB) crossing, inclusion complexes were formulated using hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HP-β-CD) and a cationic cyclodextrin polymer (TMA-poly-β-CD). These systems, exhibiting stability constants in the 103-105 M-1 range, significantly enhanced drug solubility. In vitro assays on SH-SY5Y cells demonstrated low cytotoxicity at short incubation times confirming that drug release and cellular uptake depend on CD binding affinity. In vivo biodistribution analysis through boron quantification by ICP-MS in C57BL/6 mice exhibit that intranasal administration achieves effective brain targeting while reducing systemic exposure compared to the intravenous one. Interestingly, the BMAC-9/HP-β-CD complex showed selective accumulation in Aβ plaque-rich brain areas only in APP/PS1dE9 transgenic mice. This selectivity is crucial for BNCT efficacy and offers a promising solution to the persistent challenge of targeted drug delivery in neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.title: Neuroimmune State Configurations at the Amyloid-Tau Interface in Alzheimer's Disease: A Testable Framework.
papers.abstract: Neuroimmune mechanisms are central to Alzheimer's disease (AD), but a single continuum of "more inflammation" does not explain why similar amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau burdens are associated with different clinical trajectories, tissue responses, and treatment risks. We present a testable neuroimmune-state framework that integrates, rather than replaces, the AT(N) system, cellular-phase models, and transcriptional descriptions of disease-associated microglia and reactive astrocytes. The framework treats neuroimmune states as multidimensional, regionally heterogeneous configurations defined by pathological substrate, cellular program, biological target, vascular and aging context, and measurable patient-level readouts. We distinguish four meanings of the amyloid-tau interface: a biomarker interface, a spatial tissue interface, a cellular-state interface, and a clinical-progression interface. We then examine the hypothesis of phagocytic target switching, in which clearance pathways that support plaque compaction or debris removal may, under selected tau- and complement-rich conditions, contribute to removal of stressed but potentially functional synapses. We explicitly separate evidence from longitudinal human studies, cross-sectional biomarkers, human genetics, postmortem tissue, animal models, and in vitro systems. Current biomarkers cannot yet assign patients to validated discrete neuroimmune states; proposed state readers should therefore be probabilistic, allow regional coexistence and parallel vascular-immune trajectories, and be tested for incremental value beyond established AD biomarkers and co-pathologies. Finally, we organize immune-directed interventions by clinical evidence level and frame stage matching as a research strategy rather than a treatment algorithm. The model is useful only if its predictions can be prospectively supported or falsified.

papers.title: Qi-Fu-Yin Attenuates Frailty by Regulating Gut Microbiota and Neuroendocrine Hormones in 5xFamilial Alzheimer's Disease Transgenic Mice.
papers.abstract: Frailty is a common and debilitating feature of Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet effective therapeutic strategies targeting both cognitive decline and physical frailty remain limited. Qi-Fu-Yin (QFY), a traditional Chinese herbal formulation, has been used to treat aging-related disorders, but its effects on frailty in AD and the underlying mechanisms are unclear. This study aimed to evaluate whether QFY alleviates frailty in 5xFamilial Alzheimer's Disease (FAD) transgenic mice and to explore the potential involvement of gut microbiota and neuroendocrine hormones. Mice were treated with QFY at low (2.8 g/kg), medium (5.6 g/kg), or high (11.2 g/kg) doses, or with donepezil as a positive control, for 194 days. Frailty-related behaviors were assessed using CatWalk gait analysis, grip strength, rotarod, nest-building, and aging scoring. Plasma hormone levels were measured, and fecal gut microbiota composition and function were analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing and metagenomic analysis. QFY treatment significantly improved gait parameters, grip strength, motor coordination, nesting ability, and reduced aging scores in 5xFAD mice, with effects comparable to or superior to those of donepezil. QFY also restored aberrant levels of estradiol, testosterone, and corticosterone, and reshaped gut microbiota composition, particularly by increasing the abundance of Adlercreutzia, which negatively correlated with senescence and testosterone levels. Functional metagenomics revealed that QFY partially restored disease-associated microbial pathways, including those involved in carbohydrate metabolism and virulence. These findings suggest that QFY alleviates frailty in 5xFAD mice, with effects associated with concurrent modulation of gut microbiota and neuroendocrine function, though causal relationships require further validation. These findings support further investigation of QFY as a potential intervention for AD-associated frailty.

papers.title: Multi-Dimensional Feature Adaptive Gating Network for Multi-View and Whole-Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Based Alzheimer's Disease Classification.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder associated with structural brain alterations detectable by structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI). Accurate classification of normal control (NC), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and AD remains challenging because disease-related changes are subtle, spatially distributed across multiple brain regions, and difficult to interpret in a biologically meaningful manner. Existing deep learning methods often rely on either whole-brain volumetric features or two-dimensional slice-level representations, which may limit the integration of complementary structural information and reduce model interpretability. This study presents a reproducible and explainable deep learning framework, termed the multidimensional feature adaptive gating network (MDFAG-Net), for sMRI-based AD classification and neuroimaging analysis. The framework integrates multidimensional structural MRI representations by combining 2D slice-level features extracted from sagittal, coronal, and axial views using a Vision Transformer backbone with global whole-brain features extracted using a three-dimensional convolutional neural network. An Enhanced Sparse Multiple Instance Learning module is employed to identify informative slices and suppress redundant information in long slice sequences, while an adaptive gating module dynamically fuses multiview and whole-brain features according to sample-specific feature contributions. The framework was evaluated on 842 subjects from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative dataset for NC/MCI/AD classification. MDFAG-Net demonstrated competitive classification performance and outperformed representative two-dimensional, three-dimensional, and multibranch comparison models under the same experimental setting. The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.798. Furthermore, Grad-CAM and DeepSHAP analyses revealed anatomically relevant regions associated with AD progression, including the hippocampus, amygdala, posterior cingulate gyrus, parahippocampal gyrus, and ventricular system.

papers.title: The Advanced Therapeutics for Alzheimer's Disease Review Board: A multidisciplinary model to facilitate safe access to amyloid-targeting therapies in general neurology across the Sutter Health system.
papers.abstract: Amyloid-targeting therapies (ATTs) require workup and monitoring that some general neurologists are uncomfortable with. Sutter Health treats over 3.5 million patients with more than 100 neurologists, but only 5 cognitive specialists. We developed the Advanced Therapeutics for Alzheimer's Disease (ATAD) Review Board, a system-wide model to address the shortage of specialists while enhancing safe access to ATTs across the health system. The ATAD Review Board comprises cognitive specialists, a neuroradiologist, a pharmacist, and a registered nurse program manager. Neurologists submit cases to the board for appropriate patient selection and re-review of cases with side effects. We reviewed 447 cases from 51 neurologists and 77% were eligible for treatment. The annual volume increased 148% in 2025. Total amyloid-related imaging abnormality rate was 17.4% for lecanemab and 28.8% for donanemab. We describe a system-wide review board model that supported ATT prescribing by general neurologists and expanded safe access to ATTs across a large integrated health system.

papers.title: Regional amyloid-PET clearance dynamics and anti-Aβ monoclonal antibody therapy: a preliminary real-world study.
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) is the reference biomarker for treatment target engagement in anti-amyloid beta (Aβ) therapies in early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet global metrics may mask a regional heterogeneity of amyloid clearance.
METHODS: We report real-world longitudinal amyloid-PET data from 26 patients treated with lecanemab or donanemab for 6 months. Global Centiloids and regional standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs) were quantified at baseline and 6 months and examined according to treatment, clinical diagnosis, and clinical stage.
RESULTS: Amyloid removal was regionally heterogeneous. Patients with mild cognitive impairment showed greater cortical amyloid reduction than those with mild dementia, while early- and late-onset AD exhibited comparable clearance. Frontal, anterior cingulate, and parietal regions showed the largest SUVR reductions, whereas the occipital cortex and temporal mesial cortex were consistently spared, including in patients reaching global amyloid-PET negativity.
DISCUSSION: Early amyloid clearance following anti-amyloid treatment is regionally heterogeneous and incompletely captured by global PET measures.

papers.title: Residualized occipital amyloid burden and plasma biomarker profiles in relation to ARIA-E during anti-amyloid treatment.
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Amyloid-related imaging abnormalities with edema (ARIA-E) represent the main safety concern of anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies. Whether regional amyloid topology refines ARIA-E risk in real-world practice remains unclear.
METHODS: We analyzed 31 treatment courses in early Alzheimer's disease under European Medicines Agency labeling. Residualized occipital amyloid burden was defined as observed occipital standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR) minus occipital SUVR predicted from global composite SUVR in an expanded baseline positron emission tomography derivation sample (n = 53). Associations with ARIA-E and baseline plasma biomarkers were assessed.
RESULTS: ARIA-E occurred only in the elevated occipital amyloid group: 4/13 treatment courses, versus 0/18 low or comparable courses (Fisher exact p = 0.055). All ARIA-E events involved posterior regions. The elevated pattern showed higher baseline glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), phosphorylated tau (p-tau)181, and p-tau217 levels, whereas amyloid beta 42/40 did not differ between groups. A GFAP + p-tau217 model showed exploratory discrimination of the elevated phenotype (area under the curve: 0.76).
DISCUSSION: Disproportionate occipital amyloid burden may identify a biologically vulnerable subgroup requiring validation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: Depression severity and sleep efficiency's associations with amyloid burden are additive but dependent on underlying genetic risk in late life depression.
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Evidence linking late-life depression (LLD) to amyloid beta (Aβ) burden remains mixed, possibly in part due to limited examinations of the confounding role of comorbid sleep disturbance and the moderating role of the apolipoprotein E (APOE) ɛ4 gene.
METHODS: We analyzed 110 older adults (ages 65-88, 66% female) with LLD to jointly model depression severity and sleep disturbance's relationship with Aβ, and to examine the moderating role of APOE ɛ4 genotype.
RESULTS: Depression severity, sleep efficiency, and sleep duration did not demonstrate a direct relationship with Aβ; however, a significant APOE ɛ4 moderation effect occurred for depression severity and sleep efficiency. In APOE ɛ4 carriers only, higher depression severity and lower sleep efficiency were associated with greater total Aβ burden and indicated greater likelihood of reaching clinical cutoffs for amyloid positivity. The effects of depressive symptoms and sleep efficiency were statistically unique and additive. Exploratory analyses demonstrated APOE ɛ4 also moderated the effect of lifetime duration of untreated depression on increased Aβ.
DISCUSSION: Depression severity and sleep efficiency's relationship with Aβ may be dependent on the presence of the APOE ɛ4 allele. This, among other individual differences, may partially explain mixed findings examining LLD as a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease. Furthermore, these findings do not suggest that the relationship between depression severity and amyloid is explained by the confounding role of sleep duration or sleep efficiency.

papers.title: Social determinants of health modify the association of Alzheimer's disease pathology with cognitive abilities but not of apolipoprotein E-ε4 with Alzheimer's disease pathology.
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Apolipoprotein E (APOE) -ε4 and social determinants of health (SDoH) are major Alzheimer's disease (AD) risk factors, yet whether SDoH modify the relationship between APOE-ε4, AD pathology, and cognition remains unclear.
METHODS: Using Biobank for Aging Studies (BAS) data, we assessed APOE-ε4 using polymerase chain reaction (PCR), AD pathology using immunohistochemistry, and cognitive abilities using Clinical Dementia Rating - Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB).
RESULTS: In 1,193 individuals (mean [SD] age 73.4 [13.0] years; 50.1% women; 65.4% White), APOE-ε4 carriers had higher odds of AD pathology (odds ratio [OR]: 3.95, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.85; 5.51; p < 0.001), and AD pathology was associated with poorer cognition (β = 8.07, 95% CI: 7.47; 8.67; p < 0.001). SDoH modified this pathology-cognition association (p = 0·002), which was stronger in the unfavorable (β = 9.09, 95% CI: 8.00; 10.19, p < 0.001) versus the favorable SDoH profile (β = 6.39, 95% CI: 5.42; 7.37; p < 0.001). SDoH did not modify the APOE-ε4-pathology association (p = 0.806), and no race effect modification was observed.
DISCUSSION: AD pathology was more strongly associated with poorer cognition in unfavorable SDoH profiles, highlighting SDoH as targets for AD prevention.

papers.title: Early anhedonia distinguishes behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia from Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Differentiating behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) from Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains challenging due to overlapping early behavioral and cognitive features. Anhedonia has emerged as a promising clinical marker, yet its multidimensional nature and temporal emergence across dementia syndromes remain unclear.
METHODS: Anticipatory and consummatory components of anhedonia were assessed in bvFTD and AD using the Temporal Experience of Pleasure Scale. Event-based modeling was applied in each group to stage the probabilistic emergence of anticipatory and consummatory anhedonia dimensions relative to apathy and cognitive symptoms.
RESULTS: Relative to controls, bvFTD showed marked loss of pleasure across anticipatory and consummatory components, whereas AD showed selective anticipatory anhedonia in the context of preserved consummatory pleasure. Event-based modeling placed consummatory and anticipatory anhedonia dimensions as early features of bvFTD occurring prior to overt cognitive changes. In contrast, for AD, anhedonia was probabilistically more likely to arise at later stages of the disease sequence, subsequent to cognitive decline.
DISCUSSION: These findings highlight consummatory anhedonia as an early, clinically informative marker of bvFTD and support the value of multidimensional hedonic assessment for improving dementia differentiation.

papers.title: Centrum Semiovale Perivascular Spaces Predict First Hemorrhagic Lesion in Asymptomatic Amyloid-Positive Individuals.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Identification of cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) before its hemorrhagic manifestations remains limited. We aimed to determine whether severe enlarged perivascular spaces in the centrum semiovale (EPVS-CSO) identify a prehemorrhagic stage of sporadic CAA by predicting the first appearance of CAA-related hemorrhagic lesions or incident cognitive decline in amyloid-positive, cognitively unimpaired, hemorrhage-free older adults.
METHODS: We performed a secondary analysis of the Anti-Amyloid Treatment in Asymptomatic Alzheimer's Disease (A4) trial, a phase 3 randomized study in cognitively unimpaired, amyloid-positive older adults. Participants with baseline hemorrhagic lesions were excluded. Baseline EPVS-CSO severity was dichotomized as severe versus nonsevere. Severe basal ganglia EPVS, more closely associated with hypertensive small vessel disease, was evaluated as a topographical negative-control exposure. The primary outcome was incident strictly lobar cerebral microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis. The secondary outcome was longitudinal cognitive trajectories measured by the Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite.
RESULTS: Among 932 participants (mean age 71.7 ± 4.8 years; 61.3% female), 101 (10.8%) had severe EPVS-CSO at baseline. Over a median follow up of 5.1 years (IQR 3.3-5.5 years), 33.7% of those with severe EPVS-CSO developed incident CAA-related hemorrhagic lesions compared with 13.6% of those with nonsevere EPVS-CSO (adjusted HR 2.85, 95% CI 1.91-4.25; p < 0.0001). Severe basal ganglia EPVS was not associated with incident hemorrhagic lesions (adjusted HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.35-2.18; p = 0.77). Severe EPVS-CSO was not associated with early cognitive differences, and participants who developed incident hemorrhagic lesions showed more pronounced cognitive decline.
INTERPRETATION: These findings identify severe EPVS-CSO as a strong predictor of first appearance of CAA-related hemorrhagic lesions in amyloid-positive individuals, supporting integration of amyloid biomarkers into magnetic resonance imaging-based Boston criteria. Identifying markers of the transition of CAA from a nonhemorrhagic to a hemorrhagic stage provides a potential foundation for approaching primary prevention of CAA-related hemorrhage. papers.title: The glymphatic-lymphatic axis: known pathways, open questions, and emerging roles in neurodegeneration.
papers.abstract: The discovery of the glymphatic system and meningeal lymphatic vessels has transformed our understanding of brain fluid homeostasis and central-peripheral communication, highlighting the critical role of cerebrospinal fluid in brain clearance. While substantial progress has been made in defining the structural components and physiological regulators of brain clearance, major uncertainties remain regarding (1) how these systems interact as an integrated physiological network, (2) how they fail in disease, and (3) whether they can be therapeutically manipulated. In this review, we first summarize the anatomical and physiological organization of the glymphatic-lymphatic axis, with particular emphasis on its regulatory mechanisms in light of rapid advances in this field. We then discuss how the glymphatic-lymphatic axis functionally integrates with peripheral immune and metabolic systems and describe how impairment of these clearance pathways is associated with the accumulation of pathological proteins, neuroinflammation, and vascular dysfunction and may contribute to the progression of neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases. Finally, we discuss emerging therapeutic strategies and biomarkers targeting the glymphatic-lymphatic axis. By redefining the central-peripheral crosstalk, the glymphatic-lymphatic axis provides a unifying framework for understanding brain clearance, neurodegeneration, and future therapeutic interventions.

papers.title: Advantage of cerebellar intermittent theta-burst stimulation in Alzheimer's disease (ACT-AD): study protocol for a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial.
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The cerebellum plays a crucial role in cognitive processing and thus presents a promising therapeutic target for Alzheimer's disease (AD). This trial aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of long-term, neuronavigated cerebellar intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) in patients with AD.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The ACT-AD trial is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled study involving 100 participants with mild-to-moderate AD across 4 centers in China. Participants will be randomized to receive either cerebellar iTBS or sham stimulation for 4 weeks (daily sessions), followed by 8 weeks of weekly maintenance sessions. The primary outcome is the change in the Clinical Dementia Rating Scale Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) score from baseline to week 12. Secondary outcomes include additional clinical scales. Exploratory outcomes include electroencephalogram (EEG), blood biomarkers and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Statistical analysis will follow intention-to-treat principles using mixed models for repeated measures (MMRM).
DISCUSSION: The ACT-AD trial will assess the efficacy and safety of long-term, neuronavigated cerebellar iTBS in treating patients with mild-to-moderate AD.

papers.title: Integrated physical and mental healthcare for older adults in Europe: from concept to implementation-a joint EuGMS and EAGP perspectives paper.
papers.abstract: Older adults commonly experience coexisting mental and physical multimorbidity, alongside frailty and polypharmacy. This clinical complexity is associated with poorer health outcomes, including higher rates of acute hospital admission, longer lengths of stay, increased dependency at discharge and higher mortality. Despite this, physical and mental health services for older adults are fragmented across Europe, often operating in a parallel rather than integrated manner. As a result, many patients receive poorly coordinated care. In response, there is growing interest in the development of integrated care services for these patients across Europe. Although a range of service models have been proposed, what constitutes "best practice" remains unclear and is likely to depend on local population needs, service configuration, healthcare context and healthcare workers education. The European Geriatric Medicine Society and European Association of Geriatric Psychiatry have initiated a Task and Finish Group to develop expert-based recommendations for integrated physical-mental health services for older adults across Europe. In this perspectives paper we consider the challenges associated with delivering integrated physical-mental healthcare for older adults, drawing on clinical and service level observations. We suggest that current approaches to integrated care are often limited in scope and variability and may not fully address the needs of older adults with combined physical and mental illness. A broader conceptualisation of integration may be required. We outline implications for future research, service development, and policy, with a focus on improving alignment between healthcare systems to address the needs of this growing population. This work was endorsed by the European Geriatric Medicine Society.

papers.title: Scavenger receptors associate with Alzheimer's pathology, cholesterol metabolism and synaptic dysfunction.
papers.abstract: This study investigated relationships between cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) scavenger receptors and early Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology in cognitively unimpaired older adults at elevated familial risk, with complementary analyses in autopsied frontal cortex. In the PREVENT-AD cohort, CSF levels of the scavenger receptors MSR1, SCARB2, and SCARF2 were examined in relation to AD biomarkers and synaptic proteins. Complementary analyses, with the same scavenger receptors, used frontal cortex tissue from the Douglas-Bell Canada Brain Bank and targeted sterol/oxysterol mass spectrometry. Linear regression, longitudinal mixed-effects models, pathway enrichment, and mediation analyses were performed. Higher CSF concentrations of MSR1, SCARB2, and SCARF2 were strongly associated with synaptic markers (SNAP25, SYT1, GAP43), with SCARB2 showing the strongest relationships. Associations with Tau biomarkers (t-Tau and p-Tau181) were consistently stronger than those with Aβ species, and baseline receptor levels correlated with longitudinal increases in p-Tau181 over up to 12 years. In autopsied cortex, MSR1 was increased and SCARF2 decreased in AD, while APOB, MSR1 and SCARB2 were associated specific oxysterol levels. Proteomic enrichment linked APOB to vascular and extracellular matrix pathways, whereas scavenger receptor-associated proteins were enriched for synaptogenesis, myeloid activation, and MAPK/phosphorylation signaling. Mediation analyses showed by correlation that scavenger receptors, particularly SCARB2, partially or fully mediated numerous associations between Tau biomarkers and synaptic markers (SNAP25, SYT1 and GAP43). These findings identify MSR1, SCARB2, and SCARF2 as potential integrators of lipid, immune, and synaptic processes in early AD and highlight SCARB2 as a possible mediator of Tau-associated synaptic vulnerability, supporting further mechanistic and cell type-specific investigation.

papers.title: Polysaccharide-based drug conjugates and related delivery systems for Alzheimer's disease: from molecular design to translational challenges.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) presents distinct extracellular, intracellular and vascular delivery targets, yet brain exposure of candidate therapeutics remains difficult to establish. This narrative review compares hyaluronic acid, chitosan, cyclodextrin, dextran, alginate and pectin systems by construct architecture, route, blood-brain barrier (BBB) evidence, cargo release and biological response. The literature includes covalent drug conjugates, loaded or coated carriers, host-guest complexes and intrinsically active polymers; evidence from one category cannot validate another. Clinical programs involving intravenous hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin and a transferrin-receptor antibody shuttle provide context, but do not establish BBB transport for the conjugates reviewed. We examine how polymer size and degradation influence immune safety, particularly chitosan-associated NLRP3 activation and context-dependent responses to hyaluronic acid fragments. We distinguish endothelial or whole-brain signal from parenchymal active-drug exposure, and discuss payload-specific endosomal escape. Advancement requires a defined construct, quantitative target-site exposure, target engagement, comparison with free drug and a matched carrier, and route-appropriate safety data.

papers.title: Tau phosphorylation from neuronal adaptation to Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Tau phosphorylation is classically associated with neurodegeneration, yet similar phosphorylation patterns emerge during physiological states and acute stress responses. How these overlapping patterns of phosphorylated Tau (pTau) relate to neuronal adaptation and Alzheimer's disease pathology remains unresolved. We synthesize findings from human to rodent and fly brains and from neuronal cell models, across neurodevelopment, sleep, hibernation, cellular stress, and disease. Across these contexts, pTau changes are associated with altered Tau localization and functions involving synaptic transmission, mitochondrial activity, RNA metabolism, and genomic integrity. Physiological and acute stress responses are generally transient and reversible, whereas aging, repeated stress, and amyloid-β-associated stress can promote persistent pTau accumulation, impaired clearance, aggregation, and neurodegeneration. We propose that pathological Tau phosphorylation reflects dysregulation of a shared adaptive response rather than activation of an entirely distinct pathway. The critical determinants may be phosphorylation persistence, subcellular localization, proteoform composition, and the capacity to restore Tau homeostasis.

papers.title: Anti-HDGFL2 cryptic protein antibodies provide a sensitive readout of TDP-43 pathology and clinical disease features.
papers.abstract: TAR DNA-binding protein (TDP-43) cytoplasmic aggregates and nuclear depletion contribute to TDP-43 dysfunction in frontotemporal lobar degeneration with TDP-43 pathology (FTLD-TDP) and forms of motor neuron disease (MND), particularly amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). TDP-43 regulates alternative splicing, but its dysfunction can engender the inclusion of cryptic exons (CEs) during splicing. Transcripts harboring an in-frame CE can generate de novo proteins. One example is the CE variant of hepatoma-derived growth factor-like protein 2 (HDGFL2-CE). To understand HDGFL2-CE as a readout of TDP-43 dysfunction, and its spatial relationship with TDP-43 pathology, we generate anti-HDGFL2-CE polyclonal and monoclonal antibodies and develop sensitive HDGFL2-CE immunoassays. With these tools, we observe that HDGFL2-CE accumulates in neurons with TDP-43 pathology, and that higher frontal cortex HDGFL2-CE in FTLD-TDP and FTLD-TDP/MND associates with greater pathological TDP-43, earlier age of onset, and shorter survival, supporting HDGFL2-CE as a marker tightly linked to TDP-43 dysfunction and clinical disease features.

papers.title: Tobacco-attributable burden of alzheimer's disease and other dementias in China and ASEAN: Temporal trends and projections - an observational study based on GBD 2021.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to systematically analyze the disease burden of Alzheimer's disease and other dementias (ADOD) attributed to tobacco in China and ASEAN countries from 1990 to 2021, and predict the disease burden in the next ten years to characterize the disparities in disease burden between the 2 sides, and to conduct a preliminary exploration of factors that may be associated with these disparities. Data on ADOD deaths, mortality, DALYs and DALY rates attributed to tobacco in China and ASEAN countries were extracted from GBD 2021, and the trend of disease burden was analyzed using Joinpoint regression model. R software was used for data analysis and visualization, and Joinpoint regression model was used to calculate the APC of each indicator; the disease burden attributable to tobacco in China and ASEAN countries was analyzed through the SDI; and the ARIMA was used to predict ADOD from 2022 to 2035. In China, the number of ADOD deaths (1990: 8126.47, 95% CI: 1822.19-22,577.84), mortality rate, DALYs, and DALY rate attributable to tobacco all exhibited significant and sustained upward trends from 1990 to 2021, and consistently exceeded the corresponding levels in the other ten ASEAN countries. The APC for mortality and DALY rates showed a significant increase in China and most ASEAN countries, with particularly rapid increases in mortality in China, Thailand, Cambodia, and Indonesia. Correspondingly, the DALY rate rose in most countries, indicating a growing overall disease burden. An exception was Myanmar, where the burden decreased. The burden of tobacco-attributable ADOD was consistently higher among males than females in all countries. Analysis based on SDI revealed a lower and more stable disease burden in high-SDI areas, whereas medium- and low-SDI countries demonstrated an upward trend. ARIMA model projections for 2022-2035 suggest that while mortality trends are diverse, an increasing trend is anticipated in most countries. The disease burden of ADOD attributable to tobacco use has continued to rise in China and ASEAN countries. This trend suggests a potential role for tobacco control in the prevention of ADOD, and also points to the value of strengthening tobacco regulation and paying early attention to cognitive interventions.

papers.title: A neuronal GPCR modifies neuropeptide signaling to suppress proteostasis in distal tissues.
papers.abstract: The proteostasis network (PN) safeguards the integrity of proteins by promoting various cellular activities. However, with aging, the PN's competence declines and aggregated proteins accrue within cells. This process underlies the development of neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's and Huntington's diseases. While the PN functions within cells, proteostasis is regulated across the organism by intertissue communication, which is partially governed by neurons. We previously found that reducing the expression of gtr-1, which encodes a neuronal heterotrimeric guanine nucleotide-binding protein-coupled receptor, mitigates the toxicity of the Alzheimer's disease cause, Aβ peptide. Here, we investigated the mechanism that is acted upon the knockdown of gtr-1 and found that it differentially modulates gene expression profiles, including of neuropeptide-coding genes, and dissimilarly modifies protein aggregation in worms that express distinct proteotoxic proteins. The knockdown of gtr-1 also enhances protein degradation. These findings highlight the roles of neuropeptides as organismal coordinators of proteostasis in the face of distinct proteotoxic challenges.

papers.title: DeMorph: A Decoupled Deformation Model with Anatomical Guidance for Predicting Longitudinal Brain Atrophy.
papers.abstract: Modeling the longitudinal progression of brain atrophy in Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is critical for early diagnosis and prognosis, but remains challenging for existing generative models. Current methods either fail to preserve anatomical integrity or treat progression as an entangled process, where changes from normal aging are inseparably fused with AD pathology. This fundamentally limits their scientific utility. To address this, we propose DeMorph, a novel deformation-based framework that explicitly disentangles and accurately predicts longitudinal brain MRI changes. Our transformer-based architecture features two key innovations: (1) a Decoupled Feed-Forward Network (D-FFN) for separate aging and pathology deformation pathways; and (2) a Multi-Scale Anatomical Guidance Cross-Attention (MS-AGCA) module, which explicitly injects anatomical priors to ensure spatially precise and biologically plausible disentanglement. Extensive experiments on four datasets (ADNI, OASIS-3, AIBL, and an inhouse dataset) demonstrate that DeMorph achieves stateof- the-art performance in both image similarity and anatomical accuracy. Crucially, we validate the success of our framework through robust bidirectional counterfactual synthesis, demonstrating the ability to controllably induce and remove a quantitatively plausible, AD-specific pathological effect.

papers.title: Informant Presence Fails to Enhance Alzheimer's Diagnosis in Complex Veteran Cases.
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Informant reports are thought helpful for Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnosis. We hypothesized that informants would improve diagnostic accuracy, operationalized as agreement between clinical impression and amyloid PET (aPET) findings.
METHODS: This study was a retrospective analysis of 168 Veterans referred for aPET due to diagnostic uncertainty or atypical presentation (Mage=69.3, SD=5.8). We examined the association between diagnostic accuracy and presence of an informant, patient's MoCA score, and informant type.
RESULTS: We found no evidence that informant presence was associated with diagnostic accuracy (OR = 0.92, 95% CI 0.48, 1.72), that this association varied by patient cognitive status as measured by MoCA (interaction OR = 1.13, 95% CI 0.97, 1.33), or that diagnostic accuracy differed by informant type (spouse/partner: OR = 1.23, 95% CI 0.55, 2.79; other: OR = 0.91, 95% CI 0.29, 2.71).
CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest informant presence does not necessarily enhance diagnostic accuracy for complex AD presentations. This highlights the continued value of aPET imaging in complex clinical presentations.

papers.title: Global and regional amyloid-β in explaining APOE-ε4 and sex associations with medial temporal tau: a neuropathology study.
papers.abstract: The medial temporal lobe (MTL) is a key region in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis, affected early by tau pathology. While female sex and APOE-ε4 are two known risk factors that affect tau levels, whether these factors drive tau in the MTL via amyloid-dependent or amyloid-independent mechanisms remains unclear. We investigated these relationships in two large neuropathological cohorts comprising 2550 participants from the Religious Orders Study/Memory and Aging Project (ROS/MAP; n=1587, main cohort) and Arizona Study of Aging and Neurodegenerative Disorders (AZSAND; n=963, replication cohort) covering the whole AD continuum. Neuropathological assessments of global neocortical and regional MTL amyloid-β burden were used to determine the extent to which amyloid-β pathology mediated associations of APOE-ε4 carriership and sex with MTL tau burden. In both cohorts, APOE-ε4 carriership and female sex were associated with significantly greater MTL tau pathology (all p<0.001). Adjustment for global amyloid-β attenuated but did not eliminate these associations (p≤0.024). However, after jointly accounting for global and MTL amyloid-β burden, the association between APOE-ε4 and MTL tau was no longer significant in either cohort (p≥0.19), whereas the association between female sex and MTL tau remained robust (p≤0.004). Models incorporating both global and regional MTL amyloid-β explained substantially more variance in MTL tau burden than models including only global amyloid-β, and results were replicated when further adjusting for diagnostic group or neocortical tau burden. These findings suggest that APOE-ε4 and female sex influence MTL tau accumulation through partially distinct pathogenic pathways, supporting an additional contribution of regional amyloid-β to the APOE-ε4-associated MTL tau burden while implicating additional amyloid-independent mechanisms in female vulnerability to tau accumulation.

papers.title: [Anti-amyloid antibodies against Alzheimer's disease : Lecanemab and donanemab in practice-Clinical importance, patient selection and safety management].
papers.abstract: Lecanemab and donanemab are the first disease-modifying therapies for early Alzheimer's disease. These humanized IgG1 antibodies promote the clearance of aggregated amyloid-beta peptides and, in the pivotal CLARITY AD and TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 trials, significantly delayed cognitive and functional decline, with an approximately 30% relative risk reduction for the clinical stage progression; however, the clinical meaningfulness remains contested: critics point to the small between-group difference in relation to the total score. This is weighed against the first disease-modifying effect and the first pharmacotherapy for mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer's disease. A prerequisite is the biological diagnosis: the reference standard is cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and amyloid positron emission tomography (PET), potentially complemented in the future by blood biomarkers such as plasma p‑Tau217. Amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) are the key adverse event, manageable through patient selection, ApoE-ε4 genotyping and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) monitoring. The indications and follow-up belong in specialized centers.

papers.title: Fraxetin Ameliorates Cognitive Impairment in STZ-Induced Mice: Involvement of Suppressed Microglial Hyperactivation and Improved Mitochondrial Dysfunction.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic for Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains a pressing medical challenge in the field of neuroscience. Natural compounds with structural diversity and multi-target regulatory properties have attracted increasing attention for the treatment of complex neurodegenerative disorders. ‌Fraxetin, previously identified through computer-aided virtual screening, C. elegans assays, and in vitro cellular models as a potential anti-AD natural compound, was further investigated in this study using established in vivo and in vitro systems to evaluate its efficacy in ameliorating cognitive function and elucidate underlying mechanisms. A sporadic AD mouse model was established by intracerebroventricular injection of STZ (3 mg/kg). Fraxetin (3, 10, and 30 mg/kg/day, po.) was administered until the mouse sacrifices. Cognitive performance was evaluated using the novel object recognition, passive avoidance, and Morris water maze tests. STZ induced cerebral energy metabolism disturbances accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, neuronal and synaptic loss, and cholinergic system impairment. ‌Behavioral tests confirmed that fraxetin ameliorated cognitive deficits in STZ-induced mice. Further studies revealed that fraxetin preserved mitochondrial structural integrity and enhanced mitochondrial biogenesis, accompanied by upregulation of the Sirt1/PGC-1α/Nrf1/TFAM pathway. In parallel, fraxetin attenuated microglial overactivation and neuroinflammatory responses. Consistently, in LPS-stimulated BV2 microglial cells, fraxetin inhibited nitric oxide and inflammatory mediator release, which was associated with modulation of the TLR2/MYD88/NF-κB signaling pathway, while restoring cellular bioenergetic status, indicating coordinated regulation of inflammation-associated metabolic dysfunction. Importantly, fraxetin attenuated neurodegenerative alterations in STZ-treated mice, as evidenced by reduced neuronal loss and synaptic degeneration. These effects were associated with activation of the BDNF/TrkB/ERK/CREB neurotrophic pathway and inhibition of acetylcholinesterase activity, supporting preservation of synaptic and cholinergic function. This study provides experimental evidence supporting fraxetin as a promising natural multi-target candidate for the intervention of AD.

papers.title: Greater temporo-occipital gray matter volume and frontoparietal cortical thickness in post-menopausal women: a UK Biobank study.
papers.abstract: Menopause is a critical transitional stage in women's lives, yet evidence on its impact on brain structure remains inconsistent, and large-sample neuroimaging studies are limited. Here, we applied whole-brain morphometry techniques to evaluate differences between pre- and post-menopausal women in terms of gray matter volume, cortical thickness and cortical gyrification. We processed and analyzed T1-weighted brain scans of 4098 women (1033 pre-menopausal; 3065 post-menopausal) from the UK Biobank. Post-menopausal women exhibited greater gray matter volume than pre-menopausal women primarily in the right temporal lobe, encompassing the amygdala and the hippocampus, and extending to the left temporal lobe and occipital regions. Post-menopausal women also exhibited greater cortical thickness in the frontal lobe and the supramarginal gyrus, whereas no differences in cortical gyrification were observed. These findings were consistent across multiple sensitivity analyses addressing age differences, peri-menopausal status, and other potential confounds. The spatial pattern of differences between post-menopausal and pre-menopausal women considerably overlaps with regions affected early in Alzheimer's disease, such as the medial temporal lobe and the supramarginal gyrus. Our findings of larger gray matter volume and greater cortical thickness in post-menopausal women may reflect compensatory mechanisms. Speculatively, these findings align with the biphasic model of brain structural changes in Alzheimer's disease. Further research with longitudinal designs is required to elucidate the exact mechanisms underlying the brain structural differences associated with menopause.

papers.title: Benzodiazepine use, incident dementia and Alzheimer's disease, and progression to severe dementia: A nationwide Korean cohort study.
papers.abstract: BackgroundThe association between benzodiazepine (BZD) use and dementia risk remains controversial owing to conflicting observational findings and incomplete adjustment for confounders.ObjectiveTo examine the association between BZD use and incident dementia, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), and to determine whether BZD use accelerates progression to severe dementia, using nationwide claims data with detailed comorbidity adjustment.MethodsWe conducted a matched cohort study using Korean National Health Insurance Service data, comparing 132,805 BZD users with 132,805 age- and sex-matched controls. Incident dementia (AD [F00], vascular dementia [F01], and other subtypes) was defined by ≥3 diagnostic claims within one year, and severe cases by national special-registration codes. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox models adjusted for the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) and clinical covariates.ResultsDementia incidence was 382.4/100,000 person-years in BZD users versus 280.7 in controls. BZD users had higher multimorbidity (CCI ≥7: 42.5% versus 26.5%) and psychiatric comorbidity (e.g., anxiety disorders: 42.6% versus 2.7%). After full adjustment, the HR for overall dementia attenuated from 1.43 to 1.15 (95% CI, 1.09-1.22), with similar attenuation for AD and severe dementia. The risk of progression from dementia to severe dementia was not increased among BZD users (adjusted HR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.84-1.14), with no dose- or duration-response observed.ConclusionsBZD use showed only a modest association with incident dementia, largely attributable to the higher multimorbidity burden among users, and was not associated with accelerated progression to severe dementia.

papers.title: Association between urinary metabolomics and cognitive performance in Asians with type 2 diabetes.
papers.abstract: BackgroundThere is an ongoing quest for novel biomarkers which may serve as therapeutic targets in cognitive impairment, alongside a growing appreciation of urinary metabolomics as a promising non-invasive approach to identify metabolic signature of Alzheimer's disease and other causes of dementia.ObjectiveWe studied whether urine metabolomics were associated with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and cognitive performance in a diabetic milieu.MethodsWe implemented a cross-sectional study on 1053 patients who had Type 2 diabetes (T2D). Urinary metabolites were quantitated by nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). We evaluated cognitive performance by administering Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status (RBANS). Criteria for mild cognitive impairment (MCI) were met if patients scored > 1.5 standard deviations (SDs) less than the mean RBANS score for total index or any of the cognitive domains.ResultsThe average age was 65.1 ± 7.9. Four metabolites were associated with RBANS total score after multiple testing correction by Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure in the adjusted analyses: sucrose (β = -1.17 (95%CI -1.71, -0.62)), 4-hydroxyhippurate (β = -0.92 (-1.42, -0.42)), trans-aconitate (β = -0.93 (-1.46, -0.40)), and tryptophan (β = -0.82 (-1.33, -0.32)). Sucrose was associated with MCI (OR = 2.19 (1.44, 3.32). Sucrose, trans-aconitate, 4-hydroxyhippurate, and 4-deoxythreonate were associated with delayed memory. Hypoxanthine, sucrose and tryptophan were related to visuo-spatial/constructional function.ConclusionsOur study identified several urinary metabolites which were differentially linked to cognitive performance in T2D. Future investigations are warranted to confirm the findings.

papers.title: The ACOD1-itaconate axis in anti-neuroinflammation and protection against neurodegenerative diseases.
papers.abstract: Chronic neuroinflammation mediated by activated microglia constitutes a central pathogenic mechanism underlying neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and multiple sclerosis (MS). Despite substantial progress in elucidating disease mechanisms, effective disease-modifying therapies remain elusive. Recent investigations have identified the aconitate decarboxylase 1 (ACOD1)-itaconate axis, a mitochondrial enzyme-metabolite pathway, as a critical immunometabolic checkpoint that regulates inflammation across diverse pathological contexts. This pathway exerts immunomodulatory effects through multiple mechanisms, including succinate dehydrogenase inhibition, nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 activation via Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 alkylation, and suppression of the NOD-like receptor protein 3 inflammasome. Emerging evidence has demonstrated that ACOD1-derived itaconate and its cell-permeable derivatives modulate neuroinflammation, preserve synaptic integrity, and ameliorate cognitive deficits in preclinical models of neurodegenerative diseases. This review critically synthesizes current evidence on the ACOD1-itaconate axis in central nervous system pathology, with particular emphasis on its roles in AD, PD, MS, and metabolic cognitive dysfunction. We further summarize the mechanistic insights and therapeutic potential of targeting this pathway in neuroinflammation-driven cognitive impairment. Additionally, this review uniquely integrates infection-induced and diet-induced cognitive impairment models and provides a critical perspective on translating this pathway from the bench to the bedside.

papers.title: Accelerated hippocampal atrophy in APOE ε4 homozygotes and females: Longitudinal findings from the Tohoku Medical Megabank MRI study.
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: The apolipoprotein E ε4 allele is a major genetic risk factor for Alzheimer's disease, but its longitudinal effect on hippocampal atrophy is unclear. Selective hippocampal atrophy, defined as greater hippocampal volume (HpV) loss relative to total brain volume (TBV), is an early marker of preclinical Alzheimer's disease. We examined age-related effects of APOE ε4 on longitudinal hippocampal atrophy in a large population-based cohort.
METHODS: We analyzed MRI data from 9,453 adults in the Tohoku Medical Megabank MRI Study, including 5,774 participants with follow-up MRI after a mean interval of 4.7 years. Cross-sectional analyses used linear regression to assess HpV and TBV, adjusting for age, sex, APOE genotype, and intracranial volume. Longitudinal analyses assessed HpV-Ratio and TBV-Ratio, defined as the second MRI volume divided by the first volume, using regression models including age, sex, APOE genotype, MRI interval, and interaction terms between age and APOE genotype and between age and sex. Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores obtained at the second MRI were included to assess effects independent of cognition.
RESULTS: No significant APOE genotype effects were observed in cross-sectional analyses. Longitudinally, ε4/ε4 carriers showed greater decline in HpV-Ratio than ε3/ε3 and ε3/ε4 carriers, and females showed lower HpV-Ratio than males. No APOE genotype or sex main effects were observed for TBV-Ratio. Interactions between age and APOE genotype and between age and sex demonstrated age-related acceleration of HpV-Ratio decline in ε4/ε4 carriers and females, and these effects persisted after adjustment for MoCA scores.
CONCLUSION: APOE ε4 homozygosity and female sex accelerate selective hippocampal atrophy in population-based cohorts.
